en.title: Sonnounce
en.summary: Send announcements to the Sonos speakers in your house – in your own voice. Pick the speakers you want, hold the button down while you talk, and let go. The announcement plays right away. While the announcement plays, the music is turned down, and afterwards it comes back up. The announcement itself plays at the volume the speaker is already set to. NO ACCOUNT. NO CLOUD. NO SUBSCRIPTION. The app talks directly to the speakers on your own network. The sound is recorded on the phone, and the speaker fetches it from there. Your voice never leaves the house. An announcement can be up to five minutes long. FROM YOUR WRIST With Apple Watch you can record an announcement straight from your wrist. The watch passes it on through your iPhone. SHORTCUTS Type a text in Shortcuts, and the phone reads it aloud on your speakers. It is read aloud in the language the app is set to. Use it in automations, for example when dinner is ready or when someone rings the doorbell. You can also have the most recent announcement repeated. AWAY FROM HOME With a Homey Pro you can send announcements home even when you are out. This requires the Sonnounce app to be installed on your Homey as well. If you have a VPN to your home, you can also send announcements that way. SAVE THE ANNOUNCEMENTS With a Homey you can save every announcement sent in the house. They are kept on your own Homey at home – not in the cloud – and you can download them to your iPhone. Requires Sonos speakers on the same Wi-Fi as the phone.

en.title: Airbnb is threatening to launch an AI travel agent next year
en.summary: Airbnb is developing an AI travel agent that it says will eventually be able to help plan your whole trip.
en.body:
It will be able to build an interface around your inquiry in real time.

Airbnb is planning to expand the presence of artificial intelligence features on its platform even further. The company has revealed that it's developing a new kind of AI agent, which will be designed to serve as a travel agent of sorts, in its letter for shareholders that it released with its Q3 2026 earnings. Airbnb said it's building a brand new interface that offers a custom AI experience that "builds the interface around your question."

The company said it doesn't think a "traditional chatbot is the right way to plan a trip." Its upcoming experience will populate an interface, presumably within the Airbnb app, with various elements relevant to your inquiry. The AI travel agent will be able to add maps, photos and even itineraries and comparisons to the interface in real time.

Airbnb says its agent will help you take action directly within that experience. That most likely means you'll be able to make rental bookings from the elements the agent adds to the page, but it's not clear if you'll also be able to avail of the company's other available services from the start. To note, Airbnb has launched other services within its app over the years, including grocery deliveries , car rentals and even destination-specific rentals like boats and ski gear.

"Over time, we want our agent to help guests plan their entire trip in one place, across homes, hotels, services, experiences and more," the company said. It will start rolling out the new experience to users sometime in the first half of 2027.

In addition to revealing its plans for a new AI experience, Airbnb has also discussed it newly released AI features in the letter. Just a couple of months ago, it launched AI search, which lets you make inquiries using natural language, as well as AI descriptions for listings.

en.title: At least 10 local governments have moved to drop Flock’s surveillance cameras since summer
en.summary: The concerns range from privacy to how data is shared (and with whom) to procurement concerns.
en.body:
At least 10 local governments and police departments have moved since this summer to curb, restrict, or end their use of Flock Safety technology as concerns about mass surveillance and data privacy continue to grow . The backlash is part of a broader pushback against the rapid adoption of advanced AI technology, including the data center buildout, facial recognition, and other uses of AI.

Flock, founded in 2017, sells surveillance software — like license plate readers, drones, and microphone-based edge-computing devices to pick up gunshots and other sounds — that can help solve crimes, such as finding missing people or stolen cars. More than 100,000 Flock cameras are in use nationwide.

But in the past three months, Monroe , Ohio; Newburgh , New York; Richmond , Virginia; Hopkinton, Massachusetts; New Bedford , Massachusetts; and Lansing , Michigan, have all moved to end their contracts with Flock. Meanwhile, police in East Bridgewater and Grafton, Massachusetts, also announced plans to stop using Flock cameras. Just this week, residents of League City, Texas, voted against their police department’s continued use of Flock’s license plate readers, and the cameras are now set to be removed.

The concerns range from privacy to how data is shared (and with whom) to procurement concerns.

In Asheville, North Carolina, police lost access to Flock after the city voted to terminate its contract in August, and the El Paso County Sheriff’s Office in Colorado announced in September that it would stop using Flock cameras. When asked for comment, the El Paso County Sheriff’s Office redirected TechCrunch to its press release, where Sheriff Joseph Roybal said that discontinuing the use of Flock was the right decision for the county.

“We have the tools, training, and experience to locate and apprehend criminals without relying on Flock cameras,” he said in the press release.

Tatiana Rice, a senior director for U.S. legislation at The Future of Privacy Forum, told TechCrunch that the backlash to Flock isn’t surprising and only further represents the “growing public skepticism toward technology.” Flock is a target because people can see the sensors and cameras as they drive along roads; data centers have also become physical embodiments of the resentment growing against emerging technology. “A camera at the end of your street is tangible in a way that everyday sharing and selling of personal data online is not,” Rice said.

At the state level this summer, for example, Florida barred license plate readers from state highways, while Texas paused state funding for Flock. The issues again range from data privacy concerns to misuse of the technology.

Misuse has been a real problem. In August, for example, an officer in Brentwood, Missouri was accused of using Flock cameras to stalk his ex-wife during their divorce. In September, an officer from East Texas was sentenced to prison for using Flock to stalk his ex-girlfriend and her family.

Another growing concern is how immigration officials have been able to access the technology. One case that captures the issue came in March, when Ithaca, New York, passed a resolution to terminate its contract with the Flock Group.

In the resolution, the city said there were “proven instances of Flock Safety infrastructure being used by federal agents for information purposes even without specific authorizations from the contracting locality,” and that the city had reviewed reports that “either intentionally or through its negligence,” Flock had allowed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) to “use query results from its database of state and local ALPR [automatic license plate reader] data to investigate and persecute immigrants throughout the United States.”

“Every day, police departments across the country are using Flock technology to solve serious crimes, locate suspects, find missing people, and make a measurable impact on public safety,” Flock told TechCrunch in a statement. “While we respect every community’s decision, removing a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes and protect communities moves public safety backward. Every Flock customer owns its data and controls who it is shared with and how it can be used. Flock does not sell data and does not have a contract with ICE.”

This August, Flock announced it would shorten the default period it stores data for new customers, from 30 days to seven. It also said agencies now need a case code before they can search the database.

The conversation around Flock echoes, in many ways, the fight over data centers. Many of these cities adopted Flock just a few years ago, and residents likely had no idea it was being installed, Adam Schwartz of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a digital privacy nonprofit that has investigated Flock before, told TechCrunch.

That lack of awareness is similar to how data centers are popping up across the country, often before residents understand what is happening. Schwartz said police departments often decide to use Flock on their own, with little oversight from city councils. In South Windsor , Connecticut, according to local reports, Flock cameras went live last year without public warning or a vote. In October, the town voted to remove its Flock cameras.

“Grassroots activists across the country have been demanding that city councils exercise their procurement power to refuse to pay for ALPRs,” Schwartz said, referring to councils’ power to decide what the city buys. He added that activists have been fighting for years and that “many city councils are listening.”

The main argument for technology like Flock is that it helps combat crime and keep neighborhoods safe. And many local governments are not dropping Flock or similar technology; instead, they are adding restrictions on its use or looking for alternatives.

Cleveland, Ohio, for example, voted this summer to extend its contract with Flock, but has started restricting searches related to immigration. It has also limited access to the database to the Cleveland Police alone, cutting off the Northeast Ohio Regional Fusion Center, essentially a federal intelligence agency, which had initially been given access.

“They are used and needed for investigative purposes,” the city said when reached for comment. “The Department of Public Safety is currently reviewing responses to an RFP [request for proposals] that was sent out to other vendors that provide the same technology as Flock.”

But as with data centers, communities want more say in the trade-offs. “These tools can offer real public safety benefits, but communities are clearly interested in ensuring that those benefits are not at the cost of their civil liberties,” Rice said. Surveillance technology will likely remain a political hot topic, especially since Democrats now control Congress.

In September, President Donald Trump said he liked Flock’s technology “because of law enforcement,” even though a Reuters poll that same month found that more Americans dislike the technology than like it.

Also that month, Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, introduced a bill called the Flock-Off Act to bar the use of federal money to buy “ Flock-style surveillance ” and put other safeguards in place. In October, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) introduced the Ban Flock Act to end “the rise of AI-powered surveillance cameras.”

es.title: Eva: la inteligencia artificial que adapta unas gafas inteligentes a las necesidades visuales de cada persona
es.summary: La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades para mejorar la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual. La última propuesta llega de la mano de Eyedaptic, una empresa especializada en tecnología de mejora visual que acaba de anunciar el lanzamiento de Eva, un asistente inteligente integrado en sus gafas EYE7. La principal novedad es que […] La entrada Eva: la inteligencia artificial que adapta unas gafas inteligentes a las necesidades visuales de cada persona se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades para mejorar la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual. La última propuesta llega de la mano de Eyedaptic , una empresa especializada en tecnología de mejora visual que acaba de anunciar el lanzamiento de Eva, un asistente inteligente integrado en sus gafas EYE7.

La principal novedad es que Eva no se limita a describir lo que aparece delante de la cámara. También puede interpretar lo que necesita el usuario y actuar sobre las funciones de mejora visual de las gafas.

Hasta ahora, muchas herramientas de asistencia visual basadas en inteligencia artificial se han centrado en reconocer objetos, leer textos o describir escenas. Eva pretende ir un paso más allá.

Su funcionamiento se basa en la interpretación de instrucciones expresadas mediante lenguaje natural. Esto permite que la persona pueda comunicarse con las gafas de una manera más intuitiva, sin necesidad de aprender comandos específicos.

Por ejemplo, si alguien está intentando leer un cartel y dice «no consigo leer eso», Eva puede interpretar la petición y ajustar la experiencia visual para facilitar la lectura.

De esta manera, la tecnología no solo proporciona información sobre el entorno, sino que también puede modificar determinados ajustes de las gafas para adaptarlos a la actividad que se está realizando.

Según Eyedaptic, el asistente está diseñado para ayudar en diferentes situaciones de la vida cotidiana. Entre sus aplicaciones se encuentran:

Además, la compañía indica que Eva permite comunicarse en hasta 99 idiomas, lo que amplía sus posibilidades de utilización.

Eva está integrada en las gafas EYE7 de Eyedaptic, un dispositivo que combina tecnología de visión artificial, inteligencia artificial y realidad aumentada.

Estas gafas incorporan pantallas de alta definición y diferentes funciones de mejora visual. Su objetivo es ayudar a las personas con pérdida de visión central, especialmente aquellas con enfermedades de la retina como la degeneración macular asociada a la edad (DMAE).

Una de sus características es que las funciones pueden controlarse mediante instrucciones de voz, lo que permite interactuar con el dispositivo sin tener que manejar constantemente sus controles.

La llegada de Eva refuerza esta propuesta: la inteligencia artificial puede interpretar las necesidades de la persona y actuar directamente sobre las funciones de mejora visual disponibles.

Eyedaptic ha comunicado que, durante sus pruebas internas, Eva alcanzó una precisión superior al 99 % en lectura y del 97 % en la interpretación de comandos.

La empresa también señala que el asistente ya está disponible para los usuarios de EYE7 mediante una actualización remota del software, por lo que no es necesario adquirir unas gafas nuevas para incorporar esta función.

No obstante, estas cifras deben interpretarse con cautela. Se trata de resultados comunicados por el fabricante y no de una evaluación independiente publicada en una revista científica. Será necesario conocer su funcionamiento en situaciones reales y con diferentes perfiles de discapacidad visual para valorar su utilidad.

La propuesta de Eyedaptic refleja una tendencia cada vez más presente en la tiflotecnología: desarrollar herramientas que no solo proporcionen información sobre el entorno, sino que también se adapten a las necesidades de cada persona.

Para quienes tienen baja visión, poder ajustar una ayuda visual mediante una conversación sencilla puede facilitar determinadas actividades y reducir la necesidad de navegar por menús o aprender controles específicos.

Sin embargo, estas soluciones deben entenderse como herramientas de apoyo. No recuperan la visión ni sustituyen la rehabilitación visual, las ayudas ópticas o los dispositivos de movilidad.

El verdadero potencial de Eva dependerá de su rendimiento en el día a día, de su facilidad de uso y de cómo responda a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente de la noticia: Eyedaptic .

en.title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
en.summary: Clutch, backed by Lightspeed and SignalFire, was last valued at $85 million, according to a source.
en.body:
Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security , a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source. The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies.

Palo Alto Networks and Clutch Security did not respond to a request for comment. The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions.

The high valuation is not an anomaly in a market increasingly focused on securing software against bad actors using AI to breach systems more easily. Upwind, a startup using AI to secure cloud infrastructure, recently turned down an acquisition offer from DataDog that valued it at roughly 40 times ARR, TechCrunch reported last week.

If the deal happens, it would be Palo Alto Networks’ seventh acquisition this year, according to PitchBook. The cybersecurity giant has a history of buying innovation rather than building it in-house, and it has ramped up dealmaking this year in response to rising AI-driven cyberattacks.

In September, Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, a two-year-old startup that uses AI agents to automate routine IT help desk tasks. The transaction valued Console at $500 million in stock and cash, TechCrunch reported. Other VC-backed companies that Palo Alto Networks has scooped up this year include NEA-backed Embrace, for $325 million ; Chronosphere, an observability platform backed by Greylock and Lux Capital, for $2.95 billion ; and Koi, a cyber startup backed by Battery and Team8, for $231 million , according to regulatory filings.

Several of Clutch’s competitors have also been acquired. Cyera, a cybersecurity startup valued at $12 billion earlier this year, acquired Oasis Security, which, like Clutch, focuses on managing AI agents’ access to systems, for $1 billion . Meanwhile, Cisco bought Menlo Ventures-backed Astrix for roughly $400 million , Calcalist reported.

en.title: Apple explains how to turn off the new MacBook Pro’s glowing logo
en.summary: While the illuminated Apple logo on the new MacBook Pro drew one of the biggest cheers during last week’s announcement, Apple knows that not everyone will want to keep it on. Here’s the company’s official guide to turning it off. more…
en.body:
While the illuminated Apple logo on the new MacBook Pro drew one of the biggest cheers during last week’s announcement, Apple knows that not everyone will want to keep it on. Here’s the company’s official guide to turning it off.

The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display marks the return of the illuminated Apple logo on its lid after a decade.

As Chance Miller explained in his review of the new MacBook Pro, “unlike older MacBooks, which used light from the display’s backlight to illuminate the logo, the new OLED MacBook Pro has no backlight to draw from, requiring a different approach.”

He added that, as with the old Macs, the logo’s brightness is tied to the screen brightness, though it also accounts for overall ambient brightness. He also noted that “when the MacBook Pro is closed, the logo looks like polished metal, just like it has since the 2016 redesign.”

The review echoed some of the findings developer Gui Rambo shared on X a few days ago:

Now, Apple has published an official support document that also explains how the illuminated logo works and how to turn it off completely.

Here’s Apple:

The Apple logo behind the built-in display is illuminated whenever the Mac is awake. It automatically dims or brightens based on the brightness level of the built-in screen and the lighting conditions detected by the computer’s ambient light sensor. For all screen-brightness levels, the Apple logo will be dimmer in a dim room and brighter in a bright room.

For users who’d rather keep the logo turned off at all times, Apple explains that they can run the following command in Terminal, provided they have the administrator password:

sudo defaults write com.apple.CoreBrightness LEBacklightMode -int 0

To revert the command and have the logo be illuminated again, users will need to run the following command:

sudo defaults delete com.apple.CoreBrightness LEBacklightMode

Apple notes that reinstalling macOS will also turn the logo illumination back on.

To read Apple’s full support article, follow this link . And make sure to also catch 9to5Mac’s review of the new MacBook Pro .

en.title: WhatsApp’s AI-powered photo expansion tool starts rolling out on iOS
en.summary: Select WhatsApp users on TestFlight and in the main app are now seeing the option to expand an image in the app’s photo editor. Here are the details. more…
en.body:
Select WhatsApp users on TestFlight and in the main app are now seeing the option to expand an image in the app’s photo editor. Here are the details.

iPhone users with access to Apple Intelligence have a native AI-powered photo expansion tool called Extend , which lets users pinch or drag to expand an image beyond its original borders.

This feature, which is also present on AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and image-editing platforms like Photoshop , is now also making its way into WhatsApp.

According to WABetaInfo , the platform is rolling out a Meta AI-powered image expansion tool, though it is currently limited to select users, primarily those in WhatsApp’s beta program via TestFlight.

From WABetaInfo :

When users select a photo in their chats, WhatsApp opens the drawing editor. Here, they can choose to apply some AI effect to improve it. Among these, users can find a new option to expand their photos. Once users select this option, Meta AI takes a few seconds to analyze the photo and generate the expanded version. Once the process is complete, WhatsApp shows the expanded photo in the drawing editor, and users can choose to send it. Note that this feature is also compatible with status updates.

The site notes that if the user isn’t happy with the result, they can tap an undo button to revert to the original and then try using the tool again to generate a different result.

As is usually the case with beta features on WhatsApp, there is no telling when it might become widely available.

That said, given that it has also rolled out to users in the Android beta and some users on the public iOS version already have access, a broader rollout might not be too far off.

To check out WABetaInfo ’s full report, follow this link .

en.title: Report: iPad shipments drop 27.5% as global tablet market plunges in Q3
en.summary: Despite global iPad shipments dropping 27.5% year-over-year in the third calendar quarter, Apple maintained its lead in the tablet market, according to a new report released today. Here are the details. more…
en.body:
Despite global iPad shipments dropping 27.5% year-over-year in the third calendar quarter, Apple maintained its lead in the tablet market, according to a new report released today. Here are the details.

According to a new report published by Omdia (via MacMagazine ), Apple shipped 11,5 million iPads during Q3 2026, accounting for 36% of all shipments.

Compared to Q3 2025, that was a 27.5% drop in shipments, and a 2.2 percentage-point decline in market share.

For context, the global tablet market saw a 23% year-over-year drop, with total shipments going from 41.8 million to 32.2 million units. Omdia noted this was the lowest level in nearly three years.

As for Apple’s competitors, Samsung remained in second place with 16.9% market share, followed by Lenovo with 12.7%, Xiaomi with 7.3%, and Huawei with 5.7%.

When it comes to shipment growth, Lenovo was the only company among the top five to post a positive result, up 11.9% year over year. Huawei saw the steepest decline at 43%, followed by Apple at 27.5%, Samsung at 21.7%, and Xiaomi at 10.6%.

Commenting on the results, Omdia Research Manager Himani Mukka said supply constraints are “limiting vendors’ ability to deliver meaningful specification upgrades, leaving fewer compelling differences between new models and their predecessors.”

“As a result,” she added, “consumers are increasingly expected to delay purchases until more substantial improvements become available.”

To read the full report, follow this link .

en.title: Getting the Most Out of Vispero Companion: Tips and Best Practices
en.summary: Vispero Companion has grown from a helpful question-and-answer assistant into your one conversational home for all the AI features in JAWS. Whether you want to know how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, or have a task done for you, it all happens in one familiar, accessible …
en.body:
Vispero Companion has grown from a helpful question-and-answer assistant into your one conversational home for all the AI features in JAWS. Whether you want to know how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, or have a task done for you, it all happens in one familiar, accessible window. And because everything lives in a single conversation, you can keep asking follow-up questions without starting over. Here are some tips and best practices for getting the most out of Vispero Companion.

With Vispero Companion Actions, Companion does more than answer questions. Just ask, and it can help you:

You’re always in control. Companion only works when you ask, asks for your approval before executing important steps, and stops immediately when you press ESC.

The new Vispero Companion is available through the Early Adopter Program to users in the United States who are signed in to a Vispero account. To turn it on:

Once it’s on, press JAWS KEY+SPACEBAR followed by F1 to open Companion. The JAWS key is INSERT when using Desktop Keyboard layout, and CAPS LOCK when using Laptop layout.

Companion looks at what is on your screen to understand what you’re asking about. If the application window isn’t maximized, content can be cut off at the edges, and Companion may even pick up parts of other windows, such as the taskbar. Before you ask for help, place focus in the application you are working in and press WINDOWS+UP ARROW to maximize it.

When Companion carries out a task for you, it moves to your application and works there, much as you would. If you type, click, switch windows, or open another program while it’s working, you can change what Companion sees and pull it away from the task. It’s best to leave the keyboard and mouse alone until the task is complete, and Companion will let you know what it did once it’s finished. If you need to stop it, press ESC .

Once Companion takes its first action in an application, it stays in that app for the rest of the conversation. Outlook and Word, for example, are treated as separate applications. If you want help with something in a different program such as a web browser, close Companion and relaunch it from that application.

Companion opens in its own window, just like any other application on your computer. When you’re finished with it, press ALT+F4 to close it, the same way you would close any other window.

You don’t need to know which feature or setting does the job. Just tell Companion what you need, for example:

The more detail you give, the fewer attempts Companion needs to get it right. “For example, if you are asking Companion to help you book a flight, “Set the departure date to November 14” will work better than “Select November 14,” because Companion will know which type of date you want to set.

Companion keeps track of your current conversation while it is open so you can ask a follow-up question or for the next step without starting over. When you’re ready to change topics, select New Request for a fresh start or close and then relaunch Companion from a different application.

Already have the Picture Smart and Page Explorer commands in muscle memory? Keep using them. They now bring their results right into Companion, where you can ask follow-up questions.

Companion asks before doing anything that can’t easily be undone, such as submitting a form. Take a moment to read what it’s about to do before you confirm, and check its report when the task is finished so you know exactly where things stand.

Your feedback shapes what comes next for Companion. Select Give Feedback beside New Request to rate an answer or leave a comment. This button requires the Submit Anonymous Usage Data (telemetry) option to be turned on. If you’d prefer to leave it off, email your comments to SoftwareSuggestions@vispero.com . You can also select the Send Feedback button in the JAWS Early Adopter Program dialog.

For more information and a live demo, join us for our webinar on new features of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2027 at noon ET on Thursday, November 12. Have questions? Send an email to training@vispero.com .

en.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
en.summary: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
en.body:
Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password.

The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts.

en.title: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
en.summary: Airbnb says its upcoming AI agent will help travelers plan trips, compare options, manage bookings, and get assistance throughout their stay.
en.body:
Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday , Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot.

In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month.

Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything.

“Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational. Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said.

Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would.

“What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said. “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.”

The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs.

In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself.

“Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. These are things an outside agent can’t easily do on its own,” the company wrote.

Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year.

While the company previously said to expect its AI agent sometime in the next year, it’s now more specifically committing to roll out the new technology to consumers in the first half of 2027.

The news of the agent’s release was delivered alongside strong third-quarter earnings, with revenue growing 19% to $4.87 billion, topping Wall Street estimates. It also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast, which it now predicts will be in the high teens, instead of the mid-teens.

“Airbnb is back in growth mode,” Chesky told analysts on the Q3 earnings call on Thursday. “It’s rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that’s exactly what we’re doing. Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years,” he added.

en.title: Bose recalls S1 Pro battery packs due to fire and overheating risks
en.summary: Over 670,000 units are being recalled in the US and Canada.
en.body:
Over 670,000 units are being recalled in the US and Canada.

If you own a Bose S1 Pro or S1 Pro+, we have some good news and some bad news. The good news: the speaker itself is fine. The bad news: the battery pack inside may be less than fine. Bose and the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced a recall on Thursday, covering nearly 635,000 lithium-ion battery packs in the US, as well as about 35,400 in Canada.

The affected packs can overheat and ignite, risking fire and burn injuries, so stop using yours right away if it's affected. Bose has received seven reports of batteries melting, smoking or catching fire. Among those were six cases of property damage. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported.

The S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ are Bose's portable PA speakers, designed for parties, gigs and the like. The speakers have a built-in mixer, support Bluetooth streaming and can go mobile using the removable battery pack. The S1 Pro+ supports a wireless mic and instrument transmitter, a separate $159 purchase.

The affected packs were sold from December 2017 to July 2026 at Bose, Best Buy, Amazon, Walmart and other retailers. The battery packs came in the box with many of the speaker units, which cost about $700, and were available separately for between $100 and $160.

Not every battery pack is being recalled. To find out if yours is, you'll need to remove the battery, find its 17-digit serial number, and check it against the recalled batches. If the battery's serial starts with 083723 , 078352 , 084105 , 078591 , 078592 , 084106 or 086409 , you'll want to sign up to get a free replacement on Bose's recall page . The company also provides more detailed instructions . While you wait for the replacement, you can still use the speaker on AC power.

You don't want to just toss the recalled lithium-ion batteries in the trash. Check with your local household hazardous waste center to find out how to dispose of them safely.

en.title: Google is ditching Firebase Studio soon, and it wants you to use its newer AI tools instead
en.summary: The company is going all-in on Antigravity and Google AI Studio and hopes developers will do the same.
en.body:
The company is going all-in on Antigravity and Google AI Studio.

In March, Google announced it was "sunsetting" Firebase Studio , its online integrated development environment (IDE), in favor of coding tools that put AI at the center. The company's preference for Antigravity and Google AI Studio serves its broader push around Gemini, but it also leaves anyone who liked Firebase Studio's approach in the lurch.

The ability to create new workspaces and sign up to use Firebase Studio ended on June 22, and developers have until March 22, 2027 to export their work to another IDE before it's shut down completely and all remaining data is deleted. Until then, Firebase Studio is in limbo, and deciding on an alternative largely comes down to how developers want AI to be incorporated into their development process.

Google conceived of Firebase Studio as a coding tool that could connect directly to Firebase, backend services it provides to developers that cover everything from databases to web hosting. From the launch of the IDE in 2025 , Google has imagined that AI agents would play a role in development. What's changed since then is how central AI has become. Firebase Studio offers an AI chatbot experience that can prototype and tweak apps and handle other development tasks, but the bulk of Firebase Studio is still devoted to editing code. In 2026, a growing number of coding projects start with a prompt, and thanks to the popularity of vibe coding , some users never even deal with the raw code.

Both of Google's newer coding tools, Antigravity and Google AI Studio, are designed for that reality, and since Firebase itself is sticking around and either tool can connect to it, a separate Firebase-focused IDE isn't essential. Google more or less framed its decision that way when it announced it was retiring the tool. "To streamline your workflow and make it clearer where you should start building, we're beginning the process of sunsetting Firebase Studio," the company wrote in March.

If you'd prefer to stay in Google's ecosystem, you can either switch to Google AI Studio or Antigravity. Google AI Studio is "the fastest path from prompt to full-stack production app," according to Google, which means its interface prioritizes prompts and chatting with AI. Like Firebase Studio, it's also web-based, so you can access it from any browser. In comparison, Antigravity is a desktop app that's meant to run locally on your computer. Its interface is designed for users to directly interact with their code, while also directing multiple AI agents that can work on their own. Notably, it also supports AI models other than Google's own.

Most other coding tools tend to follow a similar logic, where the coder is a team leader for agents that handle the first pass. Cursor , now owned by SpaceX, is a popular option. Both Anthropic and OpenAI also have their own AI-focused coding tools in Claude Code and Codex , respectively. Using AI in projects can come with associated costs, either in the form of subscriptions, paying for tokens, or both. Which tools developers migrate to after Firebase Studio shuts down will likely be determined as much by price as by the interface and each tool's future.

es.body:
Las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva podrán acceder a recursos de accesibilidad durante las sesiones habituales de cine gracias a soluciones como GRETA. La compañía tecnológica GRETA & STARKS y la distribuidora española ConUnPack han anunciado una alianza para impulsar el uso de esta tecnología en las salas españolas.

La iniciativa se presenta en MERCI 2026, el Mercado de Cine Independiente organizado por la Semana Internacional de Cine de Valladolid (SEMINCI) y la Asociación de Distribuidores Independientes Cinematográficos (ADICINE). El encuentro celebra su sexta edición del 28 al 30 de octubre en Valladolid.

GRETA es una aplicación móvil que permite utilizar diferentes recursos de accesibilidad sincronizados con la película. De este modo, cada espectador puede disfrutar de la sesión con los apoyos que necesita desde su propio dispositivo.

Entre sus principales funciones se encuentran:

Según explica la web oficial de GRETA , la aplicación utiliza el reconocimiento del sonido para sincronizar los recursos de accesibilidad con la película. Para utilizarla, basta con un teléfono móvil y, en el caso de la audiodescripción, unos auriculares.

Una de las principales ventajas de esta tecnología es que permite compartir una misma sesión cinematográfica sin necesidad de organizar proyecciones específicas para las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva.

Cada espectador utiliza de forma individual el recurso que necesita. Así, una persona puede escuchar la audiodescripción mientras el resto del público sigue la película con el sonido habitual de la sala. Del mismo modo, los subtítulos adaptados pueden consultarse en la pantalla del teléfono móvil.

Esta posibilidad favorece una experiencia cinematográfica compartida y contribuye a reducir las barreras de acceso a la cultura.

No obstante, es importante tener en cuenta que la aplicación no garantiza la accesibilidad de todos los títulos. Para utilizar sus funciones, la película debe contar con los recursos correspondientes y estar disponible en el catálogo.

La alianza entre GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack busca acercar estas soluciones a los profesionales de la exhibición cinematográfica en España.

Una de las ventajas del sistema es que no requiere instalar equipamiento específico en las salas para que cada usuario pueda utilizar la aplicación. Esto puede facilitar su incorporación en cines independientes y en espacios con menos recursos técnicos.

Sin embargo, la disponibilidad de películas accesibles y las condiciones de implantación del servicio siguen siendo factores importantes. Para ampliar su alcance, resulta fundamental que distribuidoras y exhibidores colaboren para ofrecer más títulos con audiodescripción y subtítulos adaptados.

La alianza se presenta en el marco de MERCI 2026, un encuentro profesional que reúne a representantes de la distribución, la exhibición y otros ámbitos de la industria audiovisual.

La programación oficial de SEMINCI incluye una presentación dedicada al cine accesible con la aplicación GRETA.

Este tipo de iniciativas pone de relieve la importancia de incorporar la accesibilidad a la distribución y exhibición cinematográfica. No basta con que una película llegue a las salas: también es necesario que las personas con diferentes necesidades sensoriales puedan acceder a su contenido.

Desde esta perspectiva, las herramientas de audio descripción y subtitulado adaptado representan un paso más hacia una cultura audiovisual inclusiva.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2027 are now available, offering new and exciting features that increase efficiency and productivity. Here’s a look at several highlights.

Vispero Companion now brings all your AI help together in one place. Whether you want to learn how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, change a setting, or have a task performed for you, just ask Vispero Companion. Because everything lives in a single conversation, you can keep asking follow-up questions without starting over.

Note: The Vispero Companion website is still available for users who need to access product guidance from devices not running JAWS.

A Vispero Account is required to use the new features in the Vispero Companion update.

This feature is part of the Early Adopter Program, which provides access to new functionality that is still under active development. It is intended for users who want to try out upcoming features and provide feedback before they are fully released.

To enable this option:

In response to frequent requests from our community, JAWS now supports MuseScore, a popular free program for writing, editing, and playing back sheet music. Composers, music students, teachers, and hobbyists all use MuseScore to create everything from simple melodies to full orchestral scores, and JAWS users can now join them.

The Smoothing tab in the Preferences dialog box is now the Smoothing and Performance tab, with a new Performance group. The default, Best text quality, uses xFont and geometric smoothing to deliver the sharpest, clearest text ZoomText and Fusion offer, along with support for legacy reading. If ZoomText or Fusion feels slow on your system, you can choose Best performance, which uses geometric smoothing only for faster response, and then return to Best text quality at any time. You can also choose this option in the Startup Wizard.

ZoomText can now magnify apps that use screen-capture protection, so you can still read content that is already shown to you on screen. This is becoming increasingly important, as:

Photo Tracking identifies people, animals, food, and other objects in an image and moves the magnified view directly from one object to the next. You no longer need to zoom and pan across the whole picture to find what you want.

All recognition happens locally on your computer, so Photo Tracking works offline and is suitable for secure environments. It is available in ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText Magnifier, and Fusion.

Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. Su experiencia, recogida en un reportaje publicado por El Periódico el 25 de octubre de 2026, pone el foco en la utilidad de estos dispositivos para ganar autonomía.

Daniel Álvarez tiene 30 años, estudia Derecho en la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) y trabaja en la ONCE. Tras perder la visión por un desprendimiento de retina irreversible, ha incorporado diferentes herramientas tecnológicas a su vida diaria.

Entre ellas destacan las gafas inteligentes, que incorporan cámaras y altavoces. Gracias a las aplicaciones compatibles, puede obtener información sobre los lugares y objetos que tiene delante.

Por ejemplo, estas gafas pueden ayudarle a distinguir si un establecimiento es un supermercado o una peluquería. También permiten leer textos, identificar colores y conocer detalles de objetos o prendas de ropa.

Sin embargo, sus posibilidades todavía tienen limitaciones. La descripción del entorno no siempre es completamente precisa y depende de la información que capta la cámara y de la interpretación que realiza el sistema.

Daniel utiliza, entre otras herramientas, ScribeMe, una aplicación que describe mediante inteligencia artificial las imágenes captadas por las cámaras de las gafas.

Las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial no se limitan a describir objetos o espacios. También pueden contribuir a mejorar la accesibilidad de documentos y materiales educativos.

En el caso de Daniel, estas herramientas le permiten adaptar información que no está disponible en un formato accesible. Por ejemplo, puede transformar gráficos de ejercicios académicos en descripciones textuales que pueda comprender mediante su lector de pantalla.

Además, utiliza la inteligencia artificial para crear aplicaciones adaptadas a sus propias necesidades.

Estas posibilidades muestran que la tecnología puede facilitar el acceso a la educación, al trabajo y a la información. No obstante, para aprovecharlas es importante que las aplicaciones y los contenidos digitales sean accesibles desde su diseño.

Aunque las gafas inteligentes ofrecen nuevas posibilidades, no sustituyen a las herramientas tradicionales de orientación y movilidad.

Daniel continúa utilizando su bastón y las técnicas de orientación que conoce. Las gafas le aportan información adicional sobre su entorno, pero no garantizan una descripción completa ni una orientación espacial precisa.

Esta distinción es importante. Reconocer un establecimiento o leer un cartel puede resultar útil durante un desplazamiento, pero no equivale a detectar todos los obstáculos ni a identificar con precisión cada elemento de la vía pública.

Por ello, es fundamental conocer las capacidades y limitaciones de cada dispositivo antes de incorporarlo a las actividades cotidianas.

El Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE ha evaluado las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta y su aplicación Meta AI para analizar su posible utilidad para personas con ceguera o discapacidad visual grave. Su evaluación constituye una referencia especializada para conocer las posibilidades de esta tecnología.

La experiencia de Daniel refleja cómo la combinación de inteligencia artificial, dispositivos inteligentes y herramientas de accesibilidad puede facilitar distintas actividades de la vida diaria.

Sin embargo, la tecnología por sí sola no elimina todas las barreras. Es necesario que las soluciones sean fiables, accesibles y adaptadas a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

También resulta importante que su desarrollo tenga en cuenta la experiencia de quienes las utilizan. La participación de las propias personas con discapacidad permite identificar necesidades concretas y mejorar la utilidad de estas herramientas.

En definitiva, las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial representan nuevas oportunidades para acceder a la información y desenvolverse con mayor autonomía. Su utilidad dependerá de que sigan mejorando y se integren como un complemento de los recursos de apoyo ya existentes.

Fuentes: El Periódico: reportaje sobre Daniel Álvarez y las nuevas tecnologías para personas con discapacidad , Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE: evaluación de las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta .

en.title: Text Dungeon: Roguelite
en.summary: A dungeon to die in, and three stories to play through. Offline, no ads. Text Dungeon is a turn-based text roguelike and a branching gamebook in one app. READ THE FIGHT Every enemy shows its next move: Attack, Heavy or Guard. Defend against a Heavy and you block all of it and get energy back. Attacking builds energy for your skills. Fights are short, and every turn is a decision. QUICK PLAY Pick a class and a perk, then go down. Eight rooms and a boss: fights, elites, traps, shops, shrines, treasure and rest. Death ends the run, and the sigils you earn unlock permanent upgrades for the next one. - Ascension: ten harder levels for every class, with bigger sigil rewards. - Class mastery: level up each class for titles and small starting bonuses. - Relic sets: collect matching relics for set bonuses. - Daily Run: one shared dungeon a day with its own twist. Keep your streak going. - Weekly Challenge: one shared run a week with stacked modifiers and its own leaderboard. - Endless: win once and the descent repeats, harder every cycle, until it kills you. - From Dec 1, the Midwinter Descent: a free winter dungeon with two new bosses. STORY MODE Make one character and carry them through a whole arc. Your choices set what happens chapters later, which characters trust you, and which ending you reach. - The Hollow Court: find out what silenced the delvers on the Hollow Road. - The Hungering Wood: the wood took Mosswick in a single season. It did not stop there. - Three Winters: 31 people, 9 barrels, and a steading across the ice that has not lit a fire in 11 days. Five oaths are offered. At most two can be kept. Four endings. The Hollow Court and Three Winters open with a free volume. Everything else is a one-time purchase, or get a whole arc in one Complete bundle. Finish an arc and its relic joins you in Quick Play. Classes: Warrior free; Rogue, Mage, Hexblade and Bloodletter in class packs. Relic packs add new items to the loot. Game Center leaderboards and achievements. NO ADS. NO ACCOUNT. NO SUBSCRIPTION. PLAYS OFFLINE. Paid content is one-time purchases. Privacy Policy: https://hipporasy.dev/roguelite/privacy/ This app uses Apple's Standard End User License Agreement (EULA): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

en.title: Into the Dungeon: Loot & Loop
en.summary: Descend deeper into the dungeon, one step at a time. Dungeon is a text-based dungeon exploration RPG. Simple controls, deep adventure. ■ Explore the Dungeon Challenge a dungeon spanning 6 underground floors. Each floor has its own theme—caves, ruins, waterways, the demon realm, forbidden depths, and the abyss beyond. Stronger monsters and rarer loot await as you descend. Watch out for traps, find healing fountains, and aim for the deepest floor. ■ Over 95 Types of Monsters Slimes, skeletons, dragons, and more inhabit each floor. Defeated enemies are recorded in your codex. ■ Rich Items & Equipment Over 190 types of items await. Equip weapons, armor, and accessories, then use alchemy to craft powerful gear from collected materials. Enhance your equipment to push its stats even further. ■ Prepare in Town • Shop: Buy and sell items • Alchemist: Combine materials into new items • Dojo: Spend gold to permanently boost your stats • Guild: Accept quests for rewards • Stash: Safely store your items ■ Codex & Lore Encountered monsters and items are recorded in your codex. Collect 100 lore fragments scattered throughout the dungeon and uncover the story of this world. ■ Two Difficulty Modes • Normal: Return to town anytime. Lose 20% gold and 2 items on defeat. • Hard: Limited town returns. Lose 50% gold, all items, and EXP on defeat—but all EXP gains are doubled. ■ Perfect For • Fans of text RPGs and roguelikes • Players who enjoy progressing in short sessions • Collectors who love filling out a codex • Anyone craving retro RPG atmosphere Pick up and play with one hand. Your next adventure awaits in the dungeon.

en.title: AXE DESCENT
en.summary: Roguelite × Turn-Based Command RPG Over 600 skills. Countless combinations. A different challenge every run. Build your own strategy from randomly presented skills and equipment. Chain skills together, combine them with equipment, and decide how to spend your limited resources. What you get may be random—but how you use it is up to you. A roguelite turn-based command RPG packed with countless choices and immense freedom. ■ Build Your Deck with Over 600 Skills There are over 600 skills to discover. Defeat enemies and choose one skill from a random selection to add to your deck. The skills you find will differ every run. Make the most of what you find, or strengthen the strategy you've already built. Shape your deck through every choice and fight your way to the deepest reaches of the Rift. ■ Weapon × Will × Potion In addition to improving your base stats by leveling up, you can equip three types of equipment: Weapons, Wills, and Potions. Combining skills and equipment can create a wide variety of powerful synergies. Each type of equipment can be upgraded at its own dedicated Facility. But you won't always have enough resources to upgrade everything to its fullest potential. Decide where to invest your limited resources and shape a build that complements your current deck. ■ Conquer the Ever-Changing Rift The Rift is the dungeon at the heart of the game, where a variety of elements change with every run. Skills obtained from enemies. Equipment found in treasure chests. NPCs encountered along the way. Facilities available during your journey. You never know exactly what you'll find, and every choice can lead your build in a new direction. Conquering Rifts rewards you with special items, unlocking new features and new stages to challenge. ■ Build Freely at the Preparation Base Before entering the Rift, the Preparation Base lets you freely customize various elements, including your starting deck and equipment. Do you build around a specific strategy from the beginning? Or create a versatile foundation and adapt to whatever you find along the way? Combine careful preparation with the unpredictable choices of each run to forge your path forward. ■ Random Encounters and Companions A variety of NPC encounters await you within the Rift. Battles, trades, events—and sometimes, the opportunity to recruit an NPC as a Companion. The abilities of your Companions are also randomized. Every encounter has the potential to change the course of your run. ■ Design Your Own Custom Skills Progress even further to unlock Custom Skills, allowing you to freely design the performance of a skill itself. Customize basic properties such as power and number of attacks, then add special effects that trigger when the skill is activated. The activation cost is calculated in detail based on the effects and values you choose, meaning more powerful effects require a greater cost. Create a single devastating strike. Combine multiple effects. Don't just choose from existing skills—create the skill you need yourself. The further you progress, the more possibilities open up for building your own unique playstyle.

en.title: AGNow,
en.summary: Audiogames usually have to be downloaded, installed and kept up to date, and most of them only run on Windows. AGNow runs them for you instead: the game runs on the server, and you hear it and play it from wherever you are, without installing anything. • Nothing to install. Games play in the browser. There are also apps for Windows, Mac and iPhone if you would rather have one. • Your own screen reader does the talking. What a game would say to NVDA is passed to the screen reader you already use, in your voice and at your speed. • Your progress is kept. Saved games stay on the server, so you can start on one device and carry on from another. • Short breaks are fine. Leave a game running and it will still be there when you get back, rather than having to be started again. It is for stepping away rather than for tomorrow, though — a game nobody comes back to is closed after a while. • Nobody has to play alone. Add friends, send messages, and let people listen in on what you are playing — or hand them a turn. • Free to play, within reason. A free account gets 12 hours of play time a month, a new one plays without a limit for its first 30 days, and there is a paid tier if you want no limit at all.

en.title: Path of Adventure 2
en.summary: When you discover a trail of old cairns, little do you know that you've just set out on the Path of Adventure. The fabled Path, though now mostly forgotten, winds through dungeons and wild lands, past monsters and traps — all the way down into the Undeep. How far will you come? - No ads - Offline - Standalone sequel (you don't need to have played part 1) Path of Adventure 2 is a text-based roguelike RPG. A unique blend of CYOA and D&D! Text-based Step into a fantasy narrative and decide how YOU want to act. Will you dare to leap over the snake pit? Explore that gloomy cave? And what will you offer the ancient statue? Roguelike The path is procedurally generated using random events, enemies and loot. Each death teaches you more about the world, bringing you closer to a well-deserved victory. RPG Develop your character's Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence, and gather the best gear to match. Manage resources, inflict status effects, and defeat monsters in turn-based combat. Easy to learn, hard to master Never played a game like this before? No problem! Just start with the tutorial and continue your journey. New characters and game modes unlock as you play; plenty of challenge awaits! Accessible Path of Adventure 2 is optimized for screen readers, thanks to the support of the community of blind and visually impaired players.

en.body:
Published 2 November 2026 by Aaron Hewitt

SandFly is a screen reader for Android phones and tablets running Android 8 or later and Wear OS watches.

With SandFly Pro:

Free features:

SandFly is free. SandFly Pro is bought in Settings > SandFly Pro, by month or by year, with prices for each country.

SandFly is distributed through GitHub releases and updates itself from them.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

SandFly is a screen reader and is used with itself; its settings, tutorial, notification list, quick settings panel and update notifications all work with SandFly. To turn it on, go to Settings > Accessibility > SandFly, after turning off any other screen reader. An interactive tutorial covers gestures and keyboard commands. Two settings need permissions that Android grants only through adb or Shizuku: Fix stuck touch exploration and Speaker when away from your ear. With Shizuku running, SandFly grants them itself; otherwise each setting shows the adb command, with a Copy command action. Problems can be reported from SandFly with Help & feedback > Report a problem.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

SandFly 0.3.0, Android 17

No accessibility ratings yet. Be the first to rate this app.

Please use this rating only for accessibility. For feedback about the app’s features, price, overall quality, or your general experience, use the comments section below.

Please log in to rate this app’s accessibility.

en.title: In-Process 2nd November 2026
en.summary: Happy All Saints Day / All Souls Day (I’m conscious of time zones, it is one of those two days for everyone, depending on where you are in the world). And wherever you are – Happy new NVDA release 🙂 Ok that was last week, but it’s like a birthday, the celebration doesn’t have to… Read More
en.body:
Happy All Saints Day / All Souls Day (I’m conscious of time zones, it is one of those two days for everyone, depending on where you are in the world). And wherever you are – Happy new NVDA release Ok that was last week, but it’s like a birthday, the celebration doesn’t have to end just because the calendar has ticked over This time around, we have:

The exciting news this time around is that NVDA 2026.3 is now available for download. This release includes significant performance improvements, improvements to NVDA’s dialogs, and expanded touch screen input.

Please note: We are aware of an issue for users of Brazilian Portuguese. We will have an update out shortly. Right now, affected users can use the NVDA 2026.3.1 Release Candidate or you can downgrade to NVDA 2026.2 .

Back to NVDA 2026.3: Several performance improvements have been made to reduce lag and improve responsiveness. NVDA now fetches and caches more information about controls in the background, improving performance in controls such as combo boxes and File Explorer. NVDA no longer causes File Explorer or other applications to crash when NVDA is exited or restarted. NVDA now recovers more quickly when an application stops responding, and will no longer freeze or flood the log with errors from unresponsive applications.

Context menus and keyboard shortcuts have been added to the Configuration Profiles, Input Gestures, and Speech Dictionaries dialogs, making these dialogs easier to use with the keyboard. It is also now possible to change an existing gesture directly in the Input Gestures dialog. The dialog used to present browsable messages has been modernized and now better supports resizing, maximizing, and minimizing.

Touch screen input has been significantly expanded. Sequential two-flick gestures now combine two flicks in quick succession into a single gesture, greatly increasing the number of bindable touch gestures. Edge gestures are also now supported, allowing gestures that start from any screen edge to be bound independently from the same gesture performed in the centre of the screen.

A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the centre of the magnified view. Windows OCR can now be used while the Screen Curtain or NVDA’s built-in Magnifier is active.

Liblouis has been updated with new Elfdalian, Sami, Maori, New Zealand Unified English Braille, Haitian Creole braille tables, a Norwegian table for Spanish text, and additional Swedish 6 and 8 dot variants. eSpeak NG has been updated with added support for Ligurian and Abkhaz.

Read the full details and download at: The NVDA 2026.3 Release Announcement .

Last fortnight we mentioned the new “Low Vision Users” page with information on various ways a low vision users might get the most out of NVDA. One big feature for this is, of course, the NVDA magnifier introduced in NVDA 2026.2. The post includes details of that, as well as including a link back to the previous blog post comparing the magnifier with the Windows magnifier , so you can judge which one will best meet your needs.

This week, I thought I’d pick out two other specific sections of that page for a closer look. Firstly, a short tip, but a useful one:

Copying information from web pages Traditionally, NVDA has only the text, not formatting or images, when copying information from web pages . It has also only worked when information was selected with the keyboard. NVDA has an option called “ Native Selection Mode ” which lets users copy formatting as well.

Importantly, if you select text with the mouse and then try to copy it with control+c , this will only work when using “Native Selection mode”. This mode can be toggled for individual pages with NVDA+shift+f10 . In NVDA 2026.3 and later, this mode can be enabled automatically in NVDA’s “Browse mode settings”.

This option in Browse mode settings is new for NVDA 2026.3 so well worth highlighting for anyone who can use it.

Visual Highlighter

NVDA’s Visual Highlight puts a border around the current object with focus, which can highlight what NVDA is reading. Press NVDA+control+g to open NVDA’s settings directly. Press control+tab to move between the different pages of settings. Use control+tab to move to the “Vision” page. The user guide describes the colours. Here are the descriptions: Solid blue highlights a combined navigator object and system focus location (e.g. because the navigator object follows the system focus) Dashed blue highlights just the system focus object Solid pink highlights just the navigator object Solid yellow highlights the virtual caret used in browse mode (where there is no physical caret such as in web browsers)

NVDA is able to move the focus around documents such as web pages where normally navigation doesn’t work. For instance, without NVDA running, you can’t arrow through a word on a web page. NVDA displays a pink line surrounding the current element with focus, such as a heading or paragraph of text. The yellow outline surrounds the character within that element which has focus (Usually the first character, unless you have moved the caret with, for instance, right arrow). A blue line surrounds the current interactive element (something you can press tab to move to). The “Basic Training for NVDA” module has more tips and techniques for navigating with the keyboard.

Screenshot of NVDA’s settings screen with a blue dotted highlight for the system focus around the “Enable Highlighting” option, and a pink highlight for the navigator object around the “Options:” heading. The mouse pointer is larger and coloured (refer to Other Windows Settings below).

We’ve made a couple of small changes to the navbar on the website this week. Hopefully all logical, but worth mentioning just in case: News: We removed the “Newsletter” and “Blog” items and replaced them with “News”. This is a menu which has options to “Subscribe” to news, check out our “Blog”, read “NVDA Stories” from users, or binge “All News Posts”. We’ve removed the “Create Account / Log In” option and in its place, the “Shop” item is a menu which lets you go to “Shop Training & Support”, “Create Account / Log In”, go to your “Cart” and “Download Purchases” (downloadable material you have previous purchased).

In addition, for those who need it, if you activate the header item for any of the navbar items with submenus (About, Get Help, News or Shop), it takes you to a page with links to each of the options for that section. What do you think? If you’ve got any feedback or any concerns, as always, please let us know.

Last fortnight we shared our new “ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” package. There has been a lot of interest in this, but I did want to cover one question we did get: Does the Accessibility Testing with NVDA package lead into the “NVDA Expert Certification”?

The answer is “No”, as they are aimed at different groups of users:

NVDA Expert Certification is aimed at users who want to prove their screen reader skills (e.g. to potential employers) or professionals who teach or support NVDA users. The exam covers the skills an end user would need to know, but which are not important for accessibility testing. A good training module to lead into this exam is “ Basic Training for NVDA ”. This module teaches things such as how to navigate around text by word, sentence and paragraph, how to search for text on a page, and copy it. It also covers using tools such as OCR or object navigation for getting around places which aren’t as accessible.

“ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” on the other hand, covers some NVDA skills, but places more emphasis on the information the screen reader is giving you which can help you ascertain the accessibility of your content. This module does not cover the finer points of searching or navigating by word, but notes the way nonvisual users can locate important information on a page, and the kinds of elements which can be useful for this. Instead of covering features for accessing inaccessible content, Accessibility Testing with NVDA highlights ways of checking that your content is accessible, and what to do if it is not.

If you are an accessibility professional who wants a way to show the world that accessibility is important to you and that you do incorporate NVDA in your testing, then we do have good news. The “ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” package includes a badge you can add to your email signature, your website or elsewhere. We encourage you to display it proudly!

That’s all for this week. We’ll be back in a fortnight with more. Do try out NVDA 2026.3 if you haven’t already. We hope you enjoy the performance and other improvements, and we look forward to sharing more highlights with you soon.

en.title: AudioGameAccess
en.summary: AudioGameAccess is a platform of games played entirely by ear, made for blind and visually impaired people. Sounds guide you, and VoiceOver tells you everything else. The games: - archery, in three levels, and bowling; - Feather Flight, a skill game; - card games: Ninety-nine, Crazy Eights, Golf, President, a colour card game, and a car race played with cards; - dice games: a five-dice game, with its combinations to fill, and Farkle; - board games: Parcheesi and Camembert Culture, a general knowledge quiz; - Four in a Row, a puzzle game: be the first to line up four tokens in an upright grid; - hangman, Sea Battle and a word game on a grid of letters; - One Word, a cooperative word game online, for 3 to 8 players: each one helps a player guess a mystery word, with a single word; - Métropole, a city-building game where you are the mayor. Every game has its own manual, in English, French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese. On iPhone, two ways to play: - with VoiceOver, the whole screen becomes the game: you play with gestures, without looking for buttons; - without VoiceOver, real buttons, cards and dice to touch, in large text and high-contrast colours for visually impaired players. Play with others: online, open a table, invite your friends or play against bots. Chat in writing and by voice, send private messages, keep a friends list and follow the leaderboards. A game can be saved and resumed later. Offline, every game but One Word can be played alone or against bots, with no account. To play online, create a free account with your email address. Other players never see it. You can block or report a player, and delete your account from the app. 3D sound on headphones places every sound around you.

en.title: Voice-enabled Makeup Assistant
en.summary: This innovative app offers audio feedback on the user’s foundation, eyeshadow and lipstick application, creating a more accessible beauty experience for the Blind and visually impaired. How It Works: The AI-powered Voice-enabled Makeup Assistant leverages machine learning and voice instruction technologies to learn your preferences and provide audio feedback when you ask. After you apply your foundation, eyeshadow or lipstick, the app will access your phone’s front camera to scan your face. Using artificial intelligence, it identifies the makeup applied to your face, eyes and lips and assesses the uniformity and boundaries of application and coverage. If there are suggested areas to touch up, the virtual assistant identifies them and makes audible recommendations so you can adjust your look. After your touch up, the app scans your face again and provides feedback on the accuracy of application.
