en.title: Set Up ZoomText and Fusion to Work the Way You Do
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday spotlighting ZoomText and Fusion features that help you be more productive at work. This is the final post in the series. Last week, we shared practical tips for tackling online tasks. This week, we’ll show you how to set up ZoomText and Fusion to work the way you do.

The features we’ve covered this month are most helpful when they’re tuned to the way you work. Taking a few minutes to customize ZoomText and Fusion is one of the most important steps you can take for workplace productivity. The right magnification level, colors, and view for each task mean less time adjusting settings and more time getting things done.

Personalized settings remove the small points of friction that add up over a busy day. When your tools are ready the moment you open an application, you can move between tasks smoothly and work more efficiently and independently. This week, we’ll look at how to save settings for each application, set up your preferred colors and display options, and use touch screen support on compatible devices.

The settings that work well in one program may not be the best choice for another. With Application Settings, you can save unique magnification and enhancement settings for each application you use. Once saved, ZoomText and Fusion automatically load the right settings as you switch between programs, so you don’t have to stop and adjust your view every time you change tasks.

To create Application Settings, open the application and adjust magnification, cursor, or mouse settings to meet your needs, then open the ZoomText menu, choose Application Settings , and save the current settings for that application. To keep your general preferences for every other program, choose Configurations > Save As Default from the ZoomText menu.

Here’s how this might look across a typical workday:

When you move from writing a report in Word to answering email in Outlook, ZoomText and Fusion switch to your Outlook settings automatically. When you come back, your Word settings are right where you left them.

The right colors can make text easier to read and reduce eye strain over a long workday. Color Enhancements let you choose from a variety of preset color schemes, such as inverted brightness or high-contrast combinations, or create your own custom colors. To pick a scheme, select the arrow next to the Color button on the Magnifier toolbar tab. Press CAPS LOCK+C to toggle color enhancements on and off. When you find a combination you like, save it as part of your default configuration or your Application Settings so it’s ready when you need it.

Different tasks also call for different views. ZoomText and Fusion offer several zoom window types for a single monitor: Full , Overlay , Lens , Line , and Docked (Top, Bottom, Left, or Right). Full magnifies the entire screen, which works well for reading documents. Docked keeps part of the screen at normal size, which can be helpful when you want to see the whole layout of an application while magnifying the area you’re working in. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the zoom window types, or select the Window button on the Magnifier toolbar tab to choose one.

If you use more than one monitor, ZoomText and Fusion can extend your workspace across two displays. When your monitors are set to extend your desktop, you can choose from these zoom window types:

In the MultiView modes, press CAPS LOCK+V to switch the active view. For more options, such as keeping both views at the same magnification level, select Window > Settings on the Magnifier toolbar tab and choose Multiple Monitor Options .

If you work on a touch screen laptop or tablet, you can control ZoomText and Fusion with gestures. Touch Screen Support works on Windows devices that support at least five simultaneous touch points.

To get started, open the ZoomText menu and choose Preferences > Touch Screen Support > Enable Touch Icon . The Touch Icon lets you switch between two modes:

Double-tap the Touch Icon with one finger to switch modes. To switch for just a moment, hold one finger on the icon, then lift it to return to the previous mode.

In ZoomText Touch Mode, try these gestures:

A few tips can make touch more comfortable at work. Choose a Touch Icon size and color that are easy for you to see from Preferences > Touch Screen Support on the ZoomText menu. Move the icon out of the way by holding one finger on it and dragging it along the edge of the screen. If you share time between a keyboard and touch, keep the icon in Windows Touch Mode when you’re tapping through applications and switch to ZoomText Touch Mode when you want to zoom or pan.

That brings our Workplace Ready series to a close. Throughout October, we’ve explored how ZoomText and Fusion can help you work more productively and independently. Here’s a look back at what we covered:

There’s always more to discover. Take some time to explore additional features and try new settings as your work changes. For tutorials, webinars, and other learning materials, visit our training page. Thank you for following along this month, and keep thriving in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

es.title: Duke investiga una IA en el móvil para mejorar la asistencia visual
es.summary: La inteligencia artificial para personas con discapacidad visual sigue avanzando. Un equipo de investigación vinculado a Duke University, en Estados Unidos, trabaja en un sistema capaz de detectar obstáculos, identificar objetos que se aproximan y describir el entorno mediante indicaciones de audio. El proyecto combina unas gafas con cámara y un teléfono móvil. Su objetivo […] La entrada Duke investiga una IA en el móvil para mejorar la asistencia visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La inteligencia artificial para personas con discapacidad visual sigue avanzando. Un equipo de investigación vinculado a Duke University, en Estados Unidos, trabaja en un sistema capaz de detectar obstáculos, identificar objetos que se aproximan y describir el entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El proyecto combina unas gafas con cámara y un teléfono móvil. Su objetivo es facilitar información útil durante los desplazamientos y otras actividades cotidianas.

Además, los investigadores quieren ejecutar el modelo de inteligencia artificial directamente en el teléfono, de esta forma, el sistema podría funcionar sin depender de servidores externos para procesar las imágenes.

La propuesta utiliza gafas inteligentes equipadas con una cámara que captura el entorno de la persona usuaria. Las imágenes se envían al sistema de inteligencia artificial para analizar lo que ocurre alrededor.

A partir de esa información, el sistema busca proporcionar indicaciones de audio sobre posibles peligros y elementos relevantes del entorno.

Entre las funciones que investiga el equipo se encuentran:

Estas funciones pretenden complementar las herramientas de movilidad existentes, como el bastón blanco o el perro guía. No buscan sustituirlas.

Una de las principales líneas de trabajo es conseguir que el sistema procese las imágenes en el propio teléfono, en lugar de enviarlas continuamente a servidores externos.

Para ello, el equipo ha trabajado con un modelo de inteligencia artificial comprimido, denominado modelo de 0,5 mil millones de parámetros. Esta reducción busca que el sistema pueda ejecutarse en un dispositivo móvil con recursos limitados.

Los investigadores han comparado un sistema básico de alertas basado en reglas con este nuevo modelo, diseñado para interpretar mejor el contexto de los posibles peligros.

Sin embargo, el equipo todavía debe completar un paso fundamental: exportar el modelo para que funcione directamente en el dispositivo. Por tanto, la asistencia inteligente sin conexión a internet es un objetivo del proyecto, no una función que deba darse por plenamente disponible.

Ejecutar la inteligencia artificial en el móvil puede ofrecer varias ventajas para las tecnologías de apoyo a la discapacidad visual.

En primer lugar, el sistema podría responder con mayor rapidez al no tener que enviar cada imagen a un servidor remoto y esperar su respuesta. En una situación de desplazamiento, reducir ese tiempo puede ser especialmente importante.

Además, el procesamiento local permitiría reducir la dependencia de una conexión a internet. Esto facilitaría el uso de determinadas funciones en lugares con poca cobertura.

Por último, mantener las imágenes en el propio dispositivo podría mejorar la privacidad, ya que reduciría la necesidad de transmitir vídeos del entorno a servidores externos. No obstante, la protección de los datos también dependerá del funcionamiento completo de la aplicación y de cómo gestione la información.

Estas ventajas son posibilidades técnicas que deberán comprobarse mediante pruebas del sistema terminado.

Aunque la investigación abre nuevas posibilidades, todavía es necesario evaluar el funcionamiento del sistema en condiciones reales.

Por ejemplo, detectar un obstáculo en una imagen no garantiza que se identifique correctamente durante un desplazamiento. Los cambios de iluminación, los espacios concurridos y los objetos difíciles de distinguir pueden afectar a los resultados.

También será importante comprobar la rapidez de las alertas, la autonomía de la batería y la facilidad de uso de las gafas. Además, los avisos deberán ser claros y oportunos para no sobrecargar de información sonora a la persona usuaria.

Por ello, las pruebas con personas ciegas y con baja visión serán fundamentales para determinar si esta tecnología aporta beneficios reales en la vida cotidiana.

La investigación de Duke University refleja una tendencia creciente en tiflotecnología: desarrollar sistemas de inteligencia artificial más pequeños y capaces de funcionar en dispositivos portátiles.

Si se consigue ejecutar el modelo directamente en el móvil, la propuesta podría reducir la dependencia de internet y facilitar respuestas más inmediatas sobre el entorno.

Aun así, el proyecto sigue en desarrollo y todavía debe demostrar su eficacia en situaciones reales. Su evolución permitirá conocer hasta qué punto la inteligencia artificial local puede complementar las ayudas de movilidad y contribuir a la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Fuentes: Duke University, Rhodes Information Initiative — Data+: AI-Powered Hazard Detection for the Visually Impaired (22 de julio de 2026)

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iMac and MacBook Pros with Performance and Connectivity Improvements, a Touchscreen for the High-End MacBook Pro, and More
en.summary: On the heels of introducing the 8th generation iPad Mini , Apple this week updated the iMac and MacBook Pro, bringing faster chips, improved connectivity, and, for the first time, a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro. iMac Featuring up to a 12-core CPU, the new iMac with M6, according to Apple's press release , delivers: Up to 2.5x faster performance in apps like Microsoft Excel, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 1.5x faster performance than M4. Up to 3.3x faster graphics performance for tasks including photo editing in Affinity, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 2x faster performance than M4. Up to 12x faster on-device AI performance for prompt processing in LM Studio, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 5x faster performance than M4. Up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing compared to M4. Up to 2x faster SSD read and write performance. With the N1 wireless networking chip, the new iMac supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and up to a 2.5 gigabit Ethernet port, included with the power adapter. The iMac with M6 is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand, 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable electricity. It can be pre-ordered from Apple in green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, blue, and silver starting today for a starting price of US $1499, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. MacBook Pro In addition to the iMac, Apple updated the base 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, N1 wireless networking chip, and up to 170 GBPS of unified memory bandwidth. The MacBook Pro with M6, according to Apple's press release delivers: Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Apple also claims the 12-core GPU paired with the dual 16-core neural engine features up to 30 percent faster graphics performance compared to M5, as well as up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads. The new MacBook Pro also features the N1 wireless networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. The MacBook Pro with M6 is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $1999, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. Apple has also introduced new high-end 14 and 16-inch MacBook Pros , bringing a thinner and lighter design, a redesigned thermal architecture, a new speaker design, hinge improvements, and, for the first time on a Mac, an OLED touchscreen and Dynamic Island. With the Dynamic Island, users will be able to view Live Activities, answer calls, and use Siri and Spotlight. At the time of publication, we do not know how VoiceOver or any other macOS accessibility tool will work with touch controls. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display continues to use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, but it now features a redesigned thermal architecture that Apple claims better redirects air away from the display, helping to prevent it from getting warm to the touch while maintaining sustained performance. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $2899, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Real world
en.summary: Welcome to Real World, created by NBM Studios! In this game, players are thrust into a 3D world full of danger and excitement. As a…
en.body:
Published 28 October 2026 by Nr Witta Draco

Welcome to Real World , created by NBM Studios! In this game, players are thrust into a 3D world full of danger and excitement. As a blind player, you must rely on your other senses and quick reflexes to navigate the environment and take down your enemies.

With a variety of weapons at your disposal, including wands for casting spells, you can hunt other players and animals, as well as dragons. If you are lucky enough to defeat the fearsome dragon, you will be rewarded with valuable items and TL, the in-game currency. But beware: the dragon respawns after 30 minutes, giving other players the chance to challenge it.

In addition to intense player-vs-player combat, the game also offers a variety of missions and challenges to complete. You can rob banks and palaces, steal valuable items, and earn extra TL. You can also take on mafia missions and defeat gangsters to earn even more rewards. As you progress through the game, you can even purchase your own hotel and use it as a base of operations. With a dynamic and constantly changing world, no two games are ever the same.

The adventure does not stop there. In Real World, players can also team up with friends and form clans to take on even more challenging missions and quests. For players who want to take their gameplay further, the game also offers a range of paid items and paid accounts that can provide additional advantages in battle.

You can create tickets to request new features or report bugs, and even marry other players if you choose. Whether you prefer to go it alone or fight alongside your clan, the choice is yours. Join the adventure and see if you have what it takes to survive in this thrilling game for blind players!

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Real world is an audio-based game designed with accessibility in mind. It includes a built-in screen reader, so TalkBack is not required while playing.

You can explore different maps, purchase weapons and other items from the in-game store using the game’s currency, and discover different areas featuring animals and other elements.

The app’s user interface is accessible, with no unlabeled buttons reported. The game is easy to use once you learn its touchscreen gestures.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

0.8.5. Android 17

No accessibility ratings yet. Be the first to rate this app.

Please use this rating only for accessibility. For feedback about the app’s features, price, overall quality, or your general experience, use the comments section below.

en.title: Announcing AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month for October 2026: ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App
en.summary: Welcome to the October 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App, a fun and relaxing water-sorting puzzle game that has quickly become one of my favorites. I know, I know. Another game for my App Pick of the Month! I realize not everyone here is a gamer, and I'm sorry for picking yet another one. But we've had so many fun new games coming our way lately, I just can't help myself! ReSort was simply too much fun to pass up. Maybe next month I'll pick something different. No promises, though! About ReSort ReSort is a puzzle game where you sort different-colored water into separate tubes until each tube contains just one color. Sounds simple enough, right? Well, it starts out that way, but things get trickier as you progress. Before long, you're moving water back and forth, trying to figure out your next move without getting yourself stuck. What I really enjoy is that there's no rush with ReSort. No timers, no move limits, and no pressure. You can take your time and figure things out at your own pace. But don't mistake relaxing for easy! Some puzzles can really get you scratching your head, and finally solving one that's been giving you trouble is incredibly satisfying. There's plenty to keep you busy, too. Along with the regular levels, ReSort offers daily puzzles with different difficulty settings and a larger Sunday challenge. You can also earn stars, work your way through different ranks, and unlock additional sounds as you progress. Accessibility is another reason ReSort stands out. The game was designed with VoiceOver in mind, with announcements for the colors and their positions in each tube. And I have to say, I absolutely love the sounds in this game! From the satisfying sound of pouring water to the little audio cues and gentle music, everything adds to the experience. It's one of those games where the sounds make playing that much more enjoyable. I also love that you can customize them to your liking. Something else I really appreciate is the developer's involvement with the AppleVis community. Since introducing ReSort in the AppleVis forum , the developer has been actively listening to feedback and making improvements. Suggestions from community members have already led to different daily puzzle difficulties, iCloud syncing, more sound options, and adjustable tube sizes for low-vision players. I love seeing developers take our community's suggestions seriously, especially when those suggestions turn into actual features so quickly. It's wonderful to see that kind of engagement. Why I'm Picking ReSort This Month For me, ReSort is just plain fun. It's easy to learn, challenging enough to keep me interested, and relaxing enough to enjoy whenever I have a few minutes to spare. And that's where the trouble starts! I'll tell myself I'm only going to play a couple of levels, and before I know it, I've played several more. There's always another puzzle waiting, and I can't seem to resist finding out whether I can solve it. I also appreciate getting to enjoy this type of game with VoiceOver. Water-sorting games have been around for years, but finding one that's this accessible isn't something I take for granted. Between the enjoyable gameplay, wonderful sounds, thoughtful accessibility, and a developer who's genuinely listening to our community, ReSort has earned its place as my October App Pick of the Month. If you enjoy puzzle games, or just want something relaxing that gives your brain a little workout, I definitely recommend giving ReSort a try. Just don't blame me if you find yourself playing longer than you planned! Download the App ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. The first 10 levels are free, with a one-time purchase to unlock the remaining levels. There are no ads or subscriptions, and all accessibility features are included for free. en.body:
Welcome to the October 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App, a fun and relaxing water-sorting puzzle game that has quickly become one of my favorites.

I know, I know. Another game for my App Pick of the Month! I realize not everyone here is a gamer, and I'm sorry for picking yet another one. But we've had so many fun new games coming our way lately, I just can't help myself! ReSort was simply too much fun to pass up. Maybe next month I'll pick something different. No promises, though!

ReSort is a puzzle game where you sort different-colored water into separate tubes until each tube contains just one color. Sounds simple enough, right? Well, it starts out that way, but things get trickier as you progress. Before long, you're moving water back and forth, trying to figure out your next move without getting yourself stuck.

What I really enjoy is that there's no rush with ReSort. No timers, no move limits, and no pressure. You can take your time and figure things out at your own pace. But don't mistake relaxing for easy! Some puzzles can really get you scratching your head, and finally solving one that's been giving you trouble is incredibly satisfying.

There's plenty to keep you busy, too. Along with the regular levels, ReSort offers daily puzzles with different difficulty settings and a larger Sunday challenge. You can also earn stars, work your way through different ranks, and unlock additional sounds as you progress.

Accessibility is another reason ReSort stands out. The game was designed with VoiceOver in mind, with announcements for the colors and their positions in each tube. And I have to say, I absolutely love the sounds in this game! From the satisfying sound of pouring water to the little audio cues and gentle music, everything adds to the experience. It's one of those games where the sounds make playing that much more enjoyable. I also love that you can customize them to your liking.

Something else I really appreciate is the developer's involvement with the AppleVis community. Since introducing ReSort in the AppleVis forum , the developer has been actively listening to feedback and making improvements. Suggestions from community members have already led to different daily puzzle difficulties, iCloud syncing, more sound options, and adjustable tube sizes for low-vision players.

I love seeing developers take our community's suggestions seriously, especially when those suggestions turn into actual features so quickly. It's wonderful to see that kind of engagement.

For me, ReSort is just plain fun. It's easy to learn, challenging enough to keep me interested, and relaxing enough to enjoy whenever I have a few minutes to spare.

And that's where the trouble starts! I'll tell myself I'm only going to play a couple of levels, and before I know it, I've played several more. There's always another puzzle waiting, and I can't seem to resist finding out whether I can solve it.

I also appreciate getting to enjoy this type of game with VoiceOver. Water-sorting games have been around for years, but finding one that's this accessible isn't something I take for granted.

Between the enjoyable gameplay, wonderful sounds, thoughtful accessibility, and a developer who's genuinely listening to our community, ReSort has earned its place as my October App Pick of the Month.

If you enjoy puzzle games, or just want something relaxing that gives your brain a little workout, I definitely recommend giving ReSort a try. Just don't blame me if you find yourself playing longer than you planned!

ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. The first 10 levels are free, with a one-time purchase to unlock the remaining levels. There are no ads or subscriptions, and all accessibility features are included for free.

Have you tried ReSort yet? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? How far have you made it in the game? I'd love to hear what you think and what other apps or games you've been enjoying this month.

es.title: TDK desarrolla un espejo ultrafino para proyectar imágenes directamente en la retina
es.summary: La empresa tecnológica TDK ha presentado un sistema que utiliza un espejo metaóptico de apenas 150 nanómetros de grosor para dirigir imágenes hacia la retina. Esta tecnología podría facilitar el desarrollo de gafas inteligentes más discretas y ligeras. El avance se dirige al mercado de las gafas inteligentes y la realidad aumentada. Además, abre nuevas […] La entrada TDK desarrolla un espejo ultrafino para proyectar imágenes directamente en la retina se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La empresa tecnológica TDK ha presentado un sistema que utiliza un espejo metaóptico de apenas 150 nanómetros de grosor para dirigir imágenes hacia la retina. Esta tecnología podría facilitar el desarrollo de gafas inteligentes más discretas y ligeras.

El avance se dirige al mercado de las gafas inteligentes y la realidad aumentada. Además, abre nuevas posibilidades para investigar futuras aplicaciones de la tiflotecnología. Sin embargo, todavía no es una ayuda visual disponible para personas con baja visión.

Los sistemas de proyección retinal dirigen haces de luz hacia la retina para generar una imagen que percibe la persona que lleva el dispositivo. De esta forma, pueden mostrar información digital sin depender exclusivamente de una pantalla convencional situada delante de los ojos.

Hasta ahora, uno de los retos de esta tecnología era el tamaño de sus componentes ópticos. Algunos sistemas necesitan espejos curvos voluminosos cerca de los ojos, lo que dificulta conseguir unas gafas con una apariencia similar a la de unas gafas convencionales.

Para resolver este problema, TDK ha desarrollado un espejo metaóptico que utiliza estructuras a escala nanométrica para controlar la reflexión de la luz. Su diseño permite integrar el componente directamente en una lente, en lugar de utilizar un espejo curvo de mayor tamaño.

El nuevo componente presentado por TDK destaca por sus dimensiones y transparencia. Según los datos publicados por la empresa, sus principales características son:

Además, el diseño pretende reducir la visibilidad de las imágenes proyectadas desde el exterior. Así, otras personas no deberían ver el contenido digital que recibe quien lleva las gafas.

Los resultados técnicos también se han recogido en un artículo publicado en SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers en septiembre de 2026. El trabajo describe la integración del espejo metaóptico en una lente y un sistema de visualización con resolución de 1.280 × 720 píxeles y un campo de visión diagonal de 45 grados.

La investigación sobre proyección retinal puede resultar relevante para el desarrollo de futuras ayudas visuales. Unas gafas con componentes ópticos más pequeños podrían facilitar la integración de información digital sin recurrir a estructuras voluminosas.

En el ámbito de la discapacidad visual, estas tecnologías podrían investigarse para mostrar información contextual, indicaciones de navegación o elementos de realidad aumentada. También podrían combinarse en el futuro con sistemas de inteligencia artificial capaces de describir el entorno o proporcionar información mediante audio.

No obstante, es importante distinguir entre las posibilidades de una tecnología y sus aplicaciones demostradas. TDK ha presentado un avance en el sistema óptico de las gafas, pero no ha demostrado que este desarrollo mejore la autonomía de personas con baja visión en situaciones cotidianas.

La utilidad para cada persona dependerá, entre otros factores, de sus necesidades visuales, las características de la imagen, el contraste, el brillo y la facilidad de uso del dispositivo completo.

Por el momento, el desarrollo de TDK se encuentra en fase de demostración tecnológica. La empresa trabaja para conseguir una versión a todo color y avanzar hacia la fabricación en serie durante los próximos años.

Por tanto, todavía no se puede hablar de un producto comercial de ayuda visual ni confirmar su precio, disponibilidad en España o utilidad clínica. También será necesario conocer las prestaciones del dispositivo completo y evaluar aspectos como la seguridad ocular, la autonomía y el funcionamiento en diferentes condiciones de iluminación.

El espejo metaóptico de TDK representa un avance en la miniaturización de los sistemas ópticos para gafas inteligentes. Su integración en una lente transparente podría ayudar a superar algunas de las barreras de diseño que han limitado el desarrollo de estos dispositivos.

Para la tiflotecnología, el interés está en comprobar si futuros sistemas basados en esta tecnología pueden ofrecer funciones realmente útiles y accesibles para las personas con discapacidad visual.

Desde EsRetina seguiremos atentos a la evolución de estas investigaciones y a las novedades que puedan traducirse en soluciones prácticas para mejorar la accesibilidad y la autonomía personal.

Fuentes: TDK: comunicado oficial sobre el sistema de proyección retinal (2 de octubre de 2026) , Mizuno y colaboradores: Direct Retinal Projection by Meta-Optic Mirror for Smart Glasses , SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers (2026) , TDK: explicación técnica del espejo metaóptico

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iPad Mini with Thinner and Lighter Design, Upgraded Display and Camera, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 Networking Chips, and More
en.summary: Apple today introduced the new 8th-generation iPad mini, bringing a thinner and lighter design, an 8.5-inch OLED display, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 networking chips, a new audio system, and more. With the new design, iPad mini features an upgraded 8.5-inch OLED display while maintaining its existing footprint, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. A new audio system that integrates components between the display and enclosure removes the speaker holes and contributes to an IP67 water and dust resistance rating, a first for any iPad. With A20 Pro, Apple claims iPad mini delivers up to 4.5X faster AI performance, up to 2.7X faster graphics performance, and up to 60 percent faster performance for everyday tasks compared to the previous generation. In addition, the N1 wireless networking chip adds Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support to iPad mini, and cellular models of the device include Apple's C2 modem, which Apple claims delivers up to 50 percent faster data speeds compared to the previous generation. The 12MP Center Stage front camera has been moved to the landscape edge of the device, as it is on other iPad models. Apple touts this as beneficial for FaceTime calls and collaboration. Apple additionally claims that the new Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and document scanning. To compliment the new iPad mini, Apple has also introduced a new Smart Folio magnetic cover that features "TechWoven" fabric. The new iPad mini is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting Wednesday, October 28 in midnight and starlight finishes for a starting price of US $699, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 with Expanded Language Support for Siri AI, Profiles for the TV App, Bug Fixes, and More
en.summary: Apple has today released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 to the public, bringing Siri AI support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, support for multiple profiles in the TV app, anniversary alerts in Call Context, and various bug fixes. Apple has also released iOS 26.7.2 for devices not running iOS 27. Resolved Accessibility Bugs Our experience is that the following accessibility bugs have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2: The changes made to VoiceOver's audio profile in iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0 appear to have been reverted. Using the Dot Pad, The f1 and f4 keys now pan the larger 20x8 display correctly. Also using the Dot Pad, the triangular-shaped buttons now pan the 20-cell display as expected. The gesture, keyboard shortcut, and Perkins-style keyboard commands for Touch and Sound Curtain once again work as expected. Navigating and selecting text with a hardware keyboard is significantly improved. VoiceOver recognizing and speaking when an item state changes or when information has updated is significantly improved, however, the issue may still occur occasionally. The buttons to switch between All and Missed in the Phone app's Classic view, as well as the ones to switch between Start Page, Bookmarks, Reading List, and History in Safari, now work. The "Clear All" rotor action in Notification Center once again works. The "Direct Touch" option in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel once again works. It is once again possible to swipe from the battery indicator to other items on the status bar when an app is opened. VoiceOver's "copy to clipboard" function now only copies the desired content rather than the full semantic markup. The Call button on the keypad in the Phone app is once again labeled correctly. The "Delete" action in the rotor for conversations in the Siri app is no longer doubled. It is no longer necessary to remove the previously-assigned command in VoiceOver Settings before a new one will work. VoiceOver once again speaks the time at the top of the hour correctly when in 24 hour mode. The "Show Bookmarks" button is once again labeled correctly when the Safari toolbar is set to "Bottom." VoiceOver now works in the "Device Diagnostics" option in the Recovery Menu. The VoiceOver per-voice equalizer now works as expected. VoiceOver once again behaves as expected when editing text and placing focus on a combo box. The Camera App no longer contains extraneous UI elements for editing camera controls when Edit Mode is not active. When swiping through the Lock Screen, VoiceOver focus once again behaves in a consistent and predictable way. In the Camera App, the VoiceOver boundary behavior now works as expected when reaching the first or last element onscreen. New Accessibility Bugs We are currently aware of two new accessibility bugs in these releases: When encountering some emojis and some pictorial icons, VoiceOver speaks them as the words "unspeakable English text." Examples of how this issue may present include: In WhatsApp, you may have a family group name which includes an emoji of adults and children holding hands. Instead of hearing "Family, man, woman and child holding hands emoji", you hear "Family, unspeakable English text". On a website, an icon with a shopping cart may say "Unspeakable English text" instead of "Shopping cart". When navigating content, VoiceOver will on occasion stop speaking, and only provide sounds and haptic feedback. This typically lasts for 20 to 30 seconds. If you notice any further changes, improvements, or regressions in your use of these releases, please post a comment below with your findings. Release Notes iOS 27.2 This update provides enhancements to Siri AI with the ability to retain useful context from previous Siri interactions as well as draw from a wider range of personal context. It also introduces Suggestions in Messages that help you take quick actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from your conversation. This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your iPhone. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List. Excluded Apps lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one setting. Granular text selection lets you select and copy just the part of a Siri response you need. Siri AI is available in more languages, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Siri AI is not available in the EU or mainland China. Other Suggestions in Messages help you take action based on the context of your conversations, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner. Shared Albums in Photos adds the ability to edit captions and comments, to avoid adding duplicate photos, and can display a reminder before albums expire so participants can save important photos and videos. Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground. The Home tab in the Podcasts app offers two separate sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing, letting you find the latest updates from your shows and then pick up where you left off. Friends tab in the Games app provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages. Simple Profiles in the Apple TV app lets everyone in your household have their own profile, with recommendations that fit what they like to watch. FaceTime supports adding a third party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call. es.summary: Tras 6 versiones beta y una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. es.body:
Tras 6 versiones beta y una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los cuadros de diálogo de NVDA y una mayor compatibilidad con la entrada mediante pantalla táctil. Se han introducido varias mejoras de rendimiento para reducir el retraso y mejorar la capacidad de respuesta. NVDA ahora recopila y almacena en caché más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, lo que mejora el rendimiento en controles como los cuadros combinados y el Explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no provoca que el Explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones se cuelguen al salir de NVDA o al reiniciarlo. Ahora, NVDA se recupera más rápidamente cuando una aplicación deja de responder y ya no se bloquea ni satura el registro con errores de las aplicaciones que no responden. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los cuadros de diálogo «Perfiles de configuración», «Gestos de entrada» y «Diccionarios del habla», lo que facilita el uso de estos cuadros de diálogo con el teclado. Ahora también es posible modificar un gesto ya existente directamente en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Se ha actualizado el cuadro de diálogo que se utiliza para mostrar los mensajes que se pueden consultar y ahora permite cambiar el tamaño, maximizar y minimizar con mayor facilidad. Se han ampliado considerablemente las opciones de introducción de datos mediante pantalla táctil. Los gestos secuenciales de dos flicks combinan ahora dos flicks consecutivos en un único gesto, lo que aumenta considerablemente el número de gestos táctiles a los que se pueden asignar acciones. Ahora también se admiten los gestos desde los bordes, lo que permite asociar gestos que se inician desde cualquier borde de la pantalla de forma independiente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para desplazar el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Ahora es posible utilizar el OCR de Windows mientras están activos la Cortina de pantalla o el magnificador integrado de NVDA. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas de braille en elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado neozelandés, criollo haitiano, una tabla noruega para texto en español y variantes adicionales suecas de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado eSpeak NG para que sea compatible con el ligur y el abjasio. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es a8a87cb823da0c62cfbae4a444ae5ae238d54dc82ad6d46d3fdb3fef082799b2. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

en.title: Access More Online with ZoomText and Fusion
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work. Last week, we followed a typical workday from Word to Teams. This week, we’ll provide practical tips for using ZoomText and Fusion when tackling online tasks.

So much of today’s work happens in a web browser: company intranets, online forms, dashboards, and web-based apps for everything from timesheets to project tracking. Whether you’re researching a topic, filling out a form, or checking the latest numbers, having ZoomText or Fusion set up to support the way you browse can make all the difference. This week, we’ll look at how these tools can help you move around websites, find information quickly, read web content comfortably, and keep an eye on the details you check most often.

Busy web pages are easier to work with when you can see exactly where you are. With ZoomText and Fusion, you can quickly adjust your magnification level or switch between different zoom window types, like Lens or Line view, to focus on the part of the page that matters most. Lens and Line are available when you use a single monitor. Lens works like a magnifying glass. It displays a magnified rectangle that follows the mouse pointer. Line works like a magnifying ruler. It displays a magnified horizontal strip that moves up and down the screen and enlarges whatever is directly beneath it.

Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the available zoom window types until you reach the one you want.

Focus enhancements highlight the item you are on as you navigate using the Tab and arrow keys through links, buttons, and form fields, making it easy to keep your place even at high magnification. Press CAPS LOCK+F to toggle focus enhancements on and off. You can also customize the appearance of the focus locator to suit your needs.

Fusion users can take advantage of the JAWS Virtual Cursor, which simulates a system cursor and lets you read and move through a web page the same way you would a document. The Virtual Cursor is on by default when you are on a web page.

Quick Navigation keys let you jump straight to the content you need without scanning the entire page. Press H to move to the next heading, F to move to the next form field, and L to move to the next list. Add SHIFT to any of these keys, such as SHIFT+H , to move backward. Press TAB to move through links and form controls.

Long pages and crowded web apps can hide the information you are trying to locate. The ZoomText Finder tool lets you search for words or phrases on web pages and in documents. Open Finder from the ZoomText toolbar, type your search term, and use the navigation buttons to jump between results. ZoomText brings each match into the magnified view, so you don’t have to pan around the page looking for it.

Fusion users can use the Find command to locate specific text on a web page. Press CTRL+F to open the Find dialog, type your search term, and press ENTER to jump to the next occurrence. Press F3 to navigate to the next occurrence of that text.

For even faster navigation, JAWS can list every link or heading on a page. Press CAPS LOCK+F7 to open the Links List or CAPS LOCK+F6 to open the Headings List, then choose an item and press ENTER to jump directly to the section or link you need.

Articles, reports, and long web pages are easier to get through when you don’t have to read every word on screen. AppReader reads documents, web pages, and email aloud while you follow along or rest your eyes. It can read from beginning to end, skim forward and backward, or read just the text you select with the mouse. AppReader reads text aloud in three modes: App View reads directly in the source application without changing your view, Text View reformats the text with your choice of fonts, colors, and magnification for easier reading, and the SpeakIt Tool reads any text on the screen that you select by clicking and dragging. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to launch App View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+T to launch Text View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+S to launch the SpeakIt Tool.

To start reading at a specific word on a web page, point to it with the mouse and press CAPS LOCK+ALT+LEFT-CLICK . Text View is especially helpful on cluttered pages, since it strips away the layout and shows just the text in a format that’s comfortable for you.

Background Reader in ZoomText lets you listen to web content while you keep working on other tasks. Select and copy the text you want to hear, then press CAPS LOCK+CTRL+B to start Background Reader. You can continue working in other applications while the content is read aloud.

Fusion users can use the JAWS Say All command to read an entire article from the cursor position. Press CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW to start continuous reading, and press CTRL to stop. This is perfect for reviewing long articles or reports.

Many of us return to the same web pages and apps every day to check a status, a total, or a notification. Reading Zones put that information one keystroke away. A reading zone is a defined area of an application window that ZoomText can display, speak, or both, at the press of a hotkey. You can set up as many as 10 zones.

To create a reading zone, open the web page or application, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+C , then drag a rectangle over the area you want the zone to cover. Give the zone a name and choose whether it should be displayed, spoken, or both.

To trigger a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+ the zone’s number (1 through 9, or 0 for zone 10). Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+N to move to the next zone and CAPS LOCK+ALT+P to move to the previous zone, or press CAPS LOCK+ALT+L to list all your zones.

For example, if you regularly check a dashboard with multiple widgets, set up Reading Zones for the most important ones. With a single keystroke, ZoomText can magnify or speak the data you need, without searching the page for it.

Join us next week as we explore how to set up ZoomText and Fusion to work the way you do, customizing settings for your workflow, preferences, and productivity. Stay tuned for more tips to help you thrive in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

en.title: What’s New In TalkBack 17.1
en.summary: Google is rolling out version 17.1 of the TalkBack screen reader. Here’s what the new version brings. Selection Mode That Works Only With Chrome It…
en.body:
Published 20 October 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Google is rolling out version 17.1 of the TalkBack screen reader . Here’s what the new version brings.

Table of Contents

It is now possible to select text outside edit boxes, but the feature is quite limited. Although Google states in the feature overview that it works on webpages, the feature is only supported in the Google Chrome browser. I tested it with Vivaldi, which is a Chromium-based browser like Google Chrome, but text selection didn’t work there.

In Chrome, you should be able to select all the text on a page or start selection mode using the assigned gesture, (by default, double-tapping and holding with two fingers). Once selection mode is active, you can select text using reading controls, as you would in edit boxes. Select all and Start selection mode are available as screen reader actions, so you can also invoke them using actions.

When I tested the feature on a webpage in Chrome, I was far from impressed. The implementation is still unreliable. Moving the focus to the next item while selecting text is not reflected in the text I cycle through using reading controls. Although the focus moves automatically when the end of the current focus is reached while selecting, the movement is not smooth and could result in having to perform the gesture several times without any text being spoken or selected. Additionally, I couldn’t find a way to pause selection without losing what has already been selected. This means you cannot select different parts of a page and append them to a single selection.

Moreover, I noticed that occasionally, I may start selection mode and hear the announcement that I am selecting by character, only to find that after I swipe down to select the next character, a larger portion of the text is selected instead.

One additional thing worth mentioning regarding selection is that it is now possible to assign gestures and keyboard shortcuts to read the selected text or to move the cursor to the start and end of the selection.

TalkBack 17.1 adds a new section to Sound and Feedback settings that allows you to select a different voice from the one you are currently using. You can also assign a gesture to open this section directly.

As is customary with Google , the feature only works with Google’s own TTS engine. When testing it with other engines, numbered voices are shown, but pressing Preview on any of them results in the TTS engine reading the text using the voice you are currently using, as if the text were simply passed to the engine. Voice selection has no effect. With Google TTS, however, voices can be changed without any issues, although I noticed that voice previews did not work during my testing.

The settings section includes an option to install more languages, which allows you to open other engines on your device. However, selecting Acapela, for example, opened the Acapela app without having any practical effect on voice selection.

For people who have been hoping to change TTS engines on the fly when a TTS engine crashes, you will be disappointed.

During the new features tour, TalkBack tells you that you can toggle Guided Vision through a button or later using the Guided Vision shortcut in the TalkBack menu. Using either of these methods does nothing. Trying the Guided Vision shortcut in the TalkBack menu several times returned me to the window I was in without toggling anything.

It is now possible to assign any TalkBack action to a braille display command. The list now extends beyond the actions included in TalkBack 17.0 to include all assignable TalkBack actions. To customize braille commands, go to Braille display settings, then Braille display commands. There, you can find all the actions that can be assigned to braille display commands, including those that are already assigned.

You can change a command if it is already assigned or assign a new command if none is assigned. You can also reset a command to its default setting or remove the assigned command.

In TalkBack 17.1, there are more fields and controls in which browse mode is turned off when using Smart Browse mode. It is also easier to take advantage of a website’s built-in keyboard shortcuts, such as using the arrow keys to expand an item in a tree view. I haven’t tested how Smart Browse mode works in the new version compared to the previous version.

It is now possible to assign a gesture to spell the current focus using Phonetic spelling, so you hear the phonetic example after hearing the letter, such as T, Tango. It is also possible to trigger Phonetic spelling by default through the Action + R + C keyboard shortcut.

More information will now be provided to help distinguish between characters on Chinese, Japanese, and Korean keyboards when using a physical keyboard.

The bug that prevented the Find Voice command from finding matching items has been fixed in the new release.

Published in General

Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 6 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 6 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 407cd4afb19d72b533c7a88a7eda86fb38d8aa753134b1000a4b6f6275fc172d. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Life In Nature
en.summary: An immersive 3D audio survival game. Craft, hunt, and explore a ruined world. Important: This is an audiogame. The game is played entirely with sound…
en.body:
Published 18 October 2026 by neirin

An immersive 3D audio survival game. Craft, hunt, and explore a ruined world.

Important: This is an audiogame. The game is played entirely with sound and has no visuals. It is designed for the blind and visually impaired community. The screen will be black during gameplay—this is intentional. Headphones are recommended for the best experience.

After a global escalation in science and military technology, the world powers engaged in a catastrophic war. Nuclear explosions altered Earth’s atmosphere, and massive solar storms destroyed all electronic systems. Most of the planet flooded, leaving survivors with only medieval-level resources to endure the harsh new world.

Developed by AudioWander, Life in Nature is a fully 3D spatial-audio multiplayer game specifically designed with accessibility in mind for blind and visually impaired players. In this unforgiving world, survival is your only goal.

Survive the Wild

Every step you take matters. You must carefully manage your Health, Energy, Hunger, and Thirst. Gather wood to build fires, hunt wild animals like bears, boars, and wolves, butcher their meat, and cook it on a skillet or spit. Find fresh water, boil it in a handmade clay pot, and make tea to restore your energy. But beware—falling from heights, animal attacks, or severe hunger will slowly drain your life.

Deep Crafting System

With electronics gone, you must rely on your hands. Gather raw materials from the earth to craft essential tools. Combine items in your hands to weave fishing nets, forge swords and crossbows, or build a sturdy wooden shelter to protect yourself. From a simple stone spear to a complex boat to cross the oceans, everything is built from scratch.

Explore Unique Maps

Navigate entirely by sound and compass directions (North, South, East, West). Explore diverse environments including the Central Valley, dense Bear and Rain forests, scorching deserts, snowy mountain peaks, and deep oceans. Dive underwater to collect oysters or explore hidden caves. Listen closely to your environment—the sound of your footsteps and the ambient noise will guide you.

Challenging Quests & Puzzles

Embark on dangerous quests like “The Lost Miner,” “A Curious Bloom,” or “The Coral Crown.” Jump across perilous chasms, climb steep cliffs, dive into deep underwater tunnels, and search for lost notes and ancient treasures hidden across the world.

Multiplayer & Combat

You are not alone in this ruined world. Meet other survivors, trade resources, and communicate via radio. If you feel brave, activate “PK Mode” (Player Kill) or join or create PK arenas to engage in high-risk, high-reward PvP combat using swords, shotguns, and shields. Team up with trusted friends to hunt dangerous predators or survive the deadly PK map.

Key Features

Put your headphones on, sharpen your senses, and start your new Life in Nature.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

When you launch the game for the first time, it will begin downloading the sounds required to play. Keep your screen reader active during this process so you can hear the download progress. If you leave the game window for any reason, the download will pause until you return.

Once the sounds have finished downloading, the game will launch. At this point, you can disable your screen reader because the game is fully self-voiced.

During account creation, there is a button that sends an account verification code to your email address. After requesting the code, reactivate your screen reader, open your email, copy the verification code, return to the game, paste it into the appropriate field, and then disable your screen reader again.

You can also use a Bluetooth keyboard if the touch gestures are difficult to use. Keyboard shortcuts are available directly from the main menu.

Before playing, make sure you read the rules in their entirety. After finishing the rules, perform a two-finger swipe down with your screen reader to locate the Accept button.

The main menu includes a button for purchasing credits. When you double-tap this button, reactivate your screen reader because the game opens Chrome or your default web browser to complete the transaction through PayPal or another supported payment service.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

2.24. Android 16

Published 18 October 2026 by Delgerbayar

Chimege Sonur is a Mongolian text reader for smartphones, developed to make Mongolian text accessible to visually impaired users. It provides Mongolian text-to-speech support so users can read on Android devices using speech output.

The project was developed by Chimege Systems as part of an initiative supporting the participation and access to services of people with disabilities in Mongolia.

Free or paid:
