es.title: Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 4 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 4 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 4 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 8be91476179710c4abffe5094459df9be1696d92e5d6cd0ace47d52321bb87ab. ¡Feliz martes!

La entrada Ya disponible la cuarta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Shortcut Menu
en.summary: Shortcut Menu lets the Android accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys, turn your choice of screen reader or other accessibility service on or…
en.body:
Published 3 October 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Shortcut Menu lets the Android accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys, turn your choice of screen reader or other accessibility service on or off. It works like the accessibility shortcut menu on iPhone:

Turning a screen reader on turns any other screen reader off, so two never talk at once. Services with the same name, such as Google’s and Samsung’s TalkBack, are told apart by their maker, such as “TalkBack (Samsung)”. Pressing the shortcut again while the menu is open closes it.

Without Shortcut Menu, a shortcut with more than one feature on it asks which one to use, and that question is not spoken when no screen reader is on.

With Shizuku, run the same command without adb shell. In Settings, Accessibility, open Shortcut Menu and turn on its shortcut, such as the volume keys. Make Shortcut Menu the only feature on that shortcut. Open the Shortcut Menu app and choose which services the menu offers. Until you choose, it offers your screen readers. The app also shows whether the permission is granted and what each shortcut is assigned to, and has a button to try the menu. How it works The shortcut turns Shortcut Menu’s accessibility service on, and the service opens the menu. When the menu closes, the service turns itself off, so the next press turns it on again. A press while the menu is open turns the service off, which closes the menu.

Choosing a service changes Android’s list of enabled accessibility services directly, so Android does not ask “Allow full control?” each time. The menu speaks with the phone’s text-to-speech engine, at the accessibility volume.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Samsung UI is the only Android UI that offers 3 accessibility shortcuts: pressing and holding the volume keys, short pressing the power and volume up keys, and the accessibility onscreen button or gesture, based on the navigation mode being used. Other OEMs offer only the first and third shortcuts. Honor even excludes the accessibility button and gesture, leaving the user with only 1 shortcut, and that shortcut can only be assigned to 1 accessibility service. On UIs that allow more than 1 accessibility service to be assigned to the shortcut, Android asks the user to choose which one to activate every time the shortcut is used. However, this dialog is not accessible if no screen reader is running.

Shortcut Menu aims to address these shortcomings by allowing the user to choose the accessibility services they want to launch from the shortcut. The user can then launch any of the selected services in an accessible way. When no screen reader is active, the service speaks the items as the user moves their finger over them, and lifting the finger activates the selected service. If a screen reader is already active, the service makes sure to turn it off before launching another screen reader to avoid potential conflicts.

Setting up the app requires an ADB command, which can be run either using ADB on a computer or directly on the phone through an ADB app that uses wireless debugging. Working with ADB is not covered here, but I personally used the ADB AppControl mobile app to enter the command that grants the app the required permission.

The app's UI is straightforward. It shows whether the permission has been granted and which shortcut is assigned to the service. It also includes a menu where you can turn services on or off without using the shortcut. The user can select which services should be included, although screen readers are checked by default. For me, Jieshuo Main, Jieshuo Helper Service, TalkBack, and AI Subtitles were all included.

When using the shortcut, the app currently speaks through Google TTS. When a screen reader is active, it behaves like a regular screen that the screen reader can interact with.

For Samsung users who keep both Samsung TalkBack and Google's TalkBack on their devices and wish to switch between them, both can be added to the services list. I haven't tested this on a Samsung device to see if there are any issues. Anyway, starting with One UI 9, Samsung TalkBack is replaced with Google TalkBack, so there are no longer two TalkBack versions.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

App version: 0.2, Android 16

★★★★★ 5.0 / 5 based on 1 rating

Please use this rating only for accessibility. For feedback about the app’s features, price, overall quality, or your general experience, use the comments section below.

Please log in to rate this app’s accessibility.

en.summary: Welcome to the September 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form . AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month: Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve Restaurant Rush is a simulation game that puts you in charge of your very own restaurant: preparing orders, serving customers (before they lose patience), earning coins, upgrading your kitchen, and building your way to different restaurants. With a 100-day campaign, Endless mode, more than 50 recipes, kitchen upgrades, and waitstaff to hire (and more), there is plenty here to keep you busy. And all of it comes from a developer who is passionate about accessibility and engagement with our community. Read more about Restaurant Rush here. New Apps Brainclash - Trivia Battle From the App Store: New here? Challenge a friend, answer whenever you wish, and let the sharpest mind win. Multiple categories, and a daily reward waiting for you. Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free Developer: Hussain Ali Brainclash on AppleVis Brainclash on the App Store Boba Sort Cafe From the App Store: Dive into the exciting world of Boba Sort Cafe! Solve charming tea & coffee sorting puzzles to relax, challenge yourself, and explore the world. This isn't just a game; it's a journey to build your global Boba Tea empire. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Electric Bear Gaming LLC Boba Sort Cafe on AppleVis Boba Sort Cafe on the App Store Chess Meets Necromancy From the App Store: Chess you already know. An army you have to raise. Chess Meets Necromancy is a turn-based roguelike played on a real chessboard with real chess movement. Your hero is one piece. Everything you capture is a corpse you can raise. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Aleksandr Myasoedov Chess Meets Necromancy on AppleVis Chess Meets Necromancy on the App Store Clipman From the App Store: Keep useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand, with accessible local history and optional encrypted synchronization through your own Clipman Server. Clipman is an accessible clipboard manager for iPhone and iPad. It keeps useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand without turning clipboard history into a complicated, mouse-first workflow. Use Clipman locally without creating an account, or connect to an optional self-hosted Clipman Server to share encrypted clipboard history between your iPhone and iPad. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Andre Louis Clipman on AppleVis Clipman on the App Store Cyphr City From the App Store: Featured in Apple's "New Games We Love". Now with the Daily Three: the same three fights for everyone, one attempt a day. Offline, ad-free, one purchase. The city runs on cards. Time to make your name. Cyphr City is a cyberpunk card RPG where poker is combat and the whole city is up for grabs. Play cards onto a 5×5 board, build poker hands (pairs, straights, flushes, full houses, and the rare royal flush) and turn every hand into damage. Both hands are face-up, so every card is a chess move: read the board, block their line, and drop the 5th card to steal a hand right out from under them. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: The Flaggship Group LLC Cyphr City on AppleVis Cyphr City on the App Store Dotball Beat The Ball From the App Store: Connect dots. Outthink the bot. Challenge a friend. Try Magic bonuses, race the clock in Rush, or sharpen your tactics in Practice. Every move changes the match. Connect dots, outthink the bot, or challenge a friend in tactical soccer. Move the ball between adjacent dots and plan around routes that have already been used. Reach one of your opponent's three goal dots to score. Put the ball in your own goal and the other side gets the goal. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: IDEAASCODE LLC Dotball Beat The Ball on AppleVis Dotball Beat The Ball on the App Store Final Fortress From the App Store: Match-3 on the screen of an old terminal. Fully playable with VoiceOver, every tile and every move is spoken. No ads, no lives, no timer. Nothing you buy helps you play. Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. The whole game is the screen of an old terminal: green text, one cursor, and you, the commandant of the last fortress. It is a quiet game. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Nothing hurries you, and nothing happens while you are away. Come back after a week and the fortress is exactly as you left it. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Dmitrii Dark Final Fortress on AppleVis Final Fortress on the App Store Game-board From the App Store: GameBoard is a premier, audio-first multiplayer gaming platform designed to bring players together through classic card and board games. Crafted with universal accessibility in mind, GameBoard is 100% compatible with native mobile screen readers like VoiceOver, while offering a visually stunning, responsive interface for all players. Play Ludo, Mile by Mile, Farkle, Citadels, and more with friends or competitors worldwide. Whether you play by sight, sound, or touch, GameBoard provides an equal, inclusive, and exciting competitive environment. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free Developer: Muamel Aljanahi Game-board on AppleVis Game-board on the App Store ghostWriter Markdown From the App Store: Bring your manuscript to life. Organize chapters, track your writing, and compile Markdown files into books, documents, presentations, and braille. ghostWriter Markdown is an accessibility-first, plain-text writing app for notes, articles, documentation, and full manuscripts. Write individual documents, organize chapters, and compile your work into a finished export. VoiceOver was at the center of the design from the first line of code. Created by a blind developer, ghostWriter gives screen reader users and anyone who loves plain text a clean, native place to write. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Marco Salsiccia ghostWriter Markdown on AppleVis ghostWriter Markdown on the App Store Hangman Blitz From the App Store: What happens when you take classic Hangman and turn up the pressure? You get Hangman Blitz, the classic word-guessing game, reimagined. Classic Hangman The game you know and love. Guess the hidden word one letter at a time, but choose carefully, you don't want to complete the figure. Timed Hangman Think you've mastered Classic? Unlock Timed Hangman and try it with a two-minute clock counting down. Guess the word before the figure is completed, or before the clock hits zero. Blitz Mode Now go all-out. The hangman figure is gone, the clock is ticking, and your goal is simple: guess as many words as you can before time runs out. Correct letters add precious seconds; mistakes take them away. Work your way through Starter, Rapid, and Extreme Blitz, where the clock gets shorter and the penalties get tougher. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is paid Developer: Cullen Gallagher Hangman Blitz on AppleVis Hangman Blitz on the App Store Honeywood: Kingdoms & Kin From the App Store: Build holdings, upgrade to Manors, and win by Harmony Points. Accessible design, haptics, and concise announcements included. Honeywood is a cozy, competitive strategy board game where you build a kingdom, grow your economy, and race to 1000 Harmony Points. Buy holdings, upgrade with buildings, and outplay your opponent through smart timing and resource control. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Amol Samant Honeywood: Kingdoms & Kin on AppleVis Honeywood: Kingdoms & Kin on the App Store Idle Dyson Swarm From the App Store: Build an automated solar empire from a single bot into a galaxy-spanning Dyson swarm. Create bots, manufacture solar panels, harness stars for energy, and reinvest your profits into an ever-growing production network. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, macOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Blindsided Games Idle Dyson Swarm on AppleVis idle Dyson Swarm on the App Store Intersector: Intersection Identifier From the App Store: Hear nearby and upcoming intersections with Intersector. Use Scan to explore your surroundings, or Live Mode for spoken updates as you walk or ride. Intersector helps you quickly identify nearby street intersections using your iPhone’s location and heading. Ask for the nearest intersection, what’s coming up ahead, use Scan Mode to point your phone down the street and hear the intersection it detects, or turn on Live Mode and have Intersector speak your upcoming intersections on a walk or during a ride with your phone locked. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, watchOS App is free Developer: Marco Salsiccia Intersector: Intersection Identifier on AppleVis Intersector: Intersection Identifier on the App Store Muse from Meta From the App Store: Muse is your personal AI agent that gets things done, always working on what matters to you. It manages email, books dinners, tracks budgets, and finds deals, with your approval. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Meta Platforms, Inc. Muse from Meta on AppleVis Muse from Meta on the App Store Nana House: Cozy Home Story From the App Store: Unpack fifty years of family memories. Every object knows where it belongs. Find its place, feel it settle, and watch the house fill with stories. No timers, no pressure. Nana's House is a quiet game about unpacking a family's memories, one room at a time. Each chapter opens a new box in a new room: a kitchen, a bathroom, a garden, a paint room, and more, each scene built carefully to hold its own place in the family's story. No timers. No scores. No wrong turns. Just a room, a box, and the feeling of setting something down in exactly the right place. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Ahmad AlBarqawi Nana House: Cozy Home Story on AppleVis Nana House: Cozy Home Story on the App Store One Line Journal app From the App Store: One sentence a day. One book at the end of the year. Your life is happening — quietly, quickly, in small moments. One Line, One Year captures 2026 as it unfolds and turns it into a beautifully structured book that's entirely yours. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free Developer: AARUSH GANESH One Line Journal app on AppleVis One Line Journal app on the App Store Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite From the App Store: New: four ball hats in the Workshop, bought with essence, and Skip now gives +3 max HP. In the Shop: Iznik, Bosphorus and Sakura themes and 8 melody packs your pegs play. Pegfall is a one-handed pegboard physics roguelite where every shot draws an orb from your deck. Aim, bounce through a living board, build ruthless combos, and descend into the Maw. NEW: PLAY WITH VOICEOVER Aim by named directions, fire with a double tap or Magic Tap, hear every volley, and inspect the board whenever you need to. Peg types use shapes as well as colour, so every board reads clearly. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: suleyman gokhan birkin Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite on AppleVis Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite on the App Store Pocket Kitchen: Cozy Cafe From the App Store: Welcome to Pocket Kitchen, a cozy cooking game where you run a small café kiosk, prepare customer orders, and turn a simple little space into your own. Take an order, head to the kitchen, and prepare a growing variety of food through clear, hands-on interactions. Make sure you choose the right ingredients, pay attention to the cooking time, serve each item when it is ready, and try not to let it burn. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is paid Developer: Loredana Lania Pocket Kitchen: Cozy Cafe on AppleVis Pocket Kitchen: Cozy Cafe on the App Store Private LLM – Local AI Chat From the App Store: Discover the Ultimate Privacy-Focused AI Assistant on iOS: Private LLM Unlock a new realm of productivity and creativity on your iPhone and iPad with Private LLM, the premier AI assistant designed with your privacy in mind. Available for a one-time purchase, it offers a range of AI capabilities without needing a subscription. Experience advanced on-device AI that keeps your interactions confidential and offline. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, macOS App is paid Developer: Numen Technologies Limited Private LLM – Local AI Chat on AppleVis Private LLM – Local AI Chat on the App Store RealTime Ai Cam From the App Store: RealTime AI Cam tells you what your camera is pointed at, out loud. Every part of it runs on the phone, so it works in airplane mode, on a subway, or in another country with no data. No account, no subscription, nothing to buy. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: NICE DREAMZ LLC RealTime Ai Cam on AppleVis RealTime Ai Cam on the App Store Remote Incident Manager Mobile From the App Store: Harness the power of born-accessible remote desktop, right in the palm of your hand! Remote Incident Manager’s mobile companion turns your iPhone or iPad into a powerful universal remote for any PC or Mac running Remote Incident Manager, opening up a world of possibilities. Tap into your home computer while on your commute, and control it as if you were right there in front of it! Run full support or training sessions straight from your phone, complete with crystal-clear voice conversations. Perform routine maintenance on machines across fleets, anytime, anywhere! Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Pneuma Solutions LLC Remote Incident Manager Mobile on AppleVis Remote Incident Manager Mobile on the App Store Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike From the App Store: One purchase, everything included. No ads, no coins to buy, no timers. A cursed House, a thumb that runs out, and one more cell you probably shouldn't touch. A scratch-card roguelike. You work the night counter of a House that sells luck sealed under foil. The quota is due by dawn. Miss it, and the House keeps you. Every ticket is a grid of foil hiding cash, multipliers and skulls. Your thumb is the budget — stamina runs out long before the tickets do, so where you scratch matters as much as what's under it. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is paid Developer: Adam Gelatka Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike on AppleVis Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike on the App Store Six Hollows: Auto Battler From the App Store: Draft one item a round and watch your tree fight five rival ghosts. Blood Moon runs all October: deeper Bleed and Halloween rewards to earn. Free to play, no ads. Six trees walk into the forest. One walks out. Make sure it is yours. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: CODE IN MOTION S.R.L. Six Hollows: Auto Battler on AppleVis Six Hollows: Auto Battler on the App Store Verbena From the App Store: Verbena — a cozy word roguelike. Spell words. Grow your garden. Chase the bloom. Verbena blends the calm of a cozy garden with the moreish "just one more run" Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Naizhong Xu Verbena on AppleVis Verbena on the App Store VoiceGammon From the App Store: VoiceGammon brings Portes — one of the three traditional Greek backgammon games — to everyone, with particular care for VoiceOver accessibility. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is paid Developer: Stelios Platsis VoiceGammon on AppleVis VoiceGammon on the App Store All recent app entries may be found at: iOS/iPadOS Mac Apple Watch Apple TV Notable App Updates Dolphin EasyReader From the App Store: Open a World of Accessible Books EasyReader removes barriers to reading, enabling anyone with a print disability to read independently. Global links to over 50 libraries connects you to millions of titles and empowers you to read in ways that work best for you. EasyReader offers a customisable reading experience and supports a wide range of accessibility needs including dyslexia and vision impairment. Below is a summary of recent updates to Dolphin EasyReader. Please see the App Store page for full release notes. Improved audiobook reader view Improved audiobook layout for easier navigation with assistive technology Options to skip back and forward are now located in reader view New word spacing controls for improved readability Fixed an issue that required users to sign into library services each time they opened the app Fixed an issue that caused the app to crash when adding a bookmark in the audiobook layout Bug fixes and accessibility improvements Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, macOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Dolphin Computer Access Ltd Dolphin EasyReader on AppleVis Dolphin EasyReader on the App Store Earshot Podcasts From the App Store: Earshot is a podcast player built accessibility-first. Every screen, button, and gesture works fully with VoiceOver, so blind and low-vision listeners get the same fast, complete experience as everyone else. Below is a summary of recent updates to Earshot Podcasts. Please see the App Store page for full release notes. Added ability to brows Apple Podcasts directory without following a show Improved podcast search and filtering to improve speed and organization New ways to organize episode cues Improved transcript viewing and exporting experience Added ability to skip forward or backward with Siri and Shortcuts Added ability to customize VoiceOver verbosity for podcasts and individual episodes Added ability to change playback speed Added ability to give podcasts custom display names in the library Added sleep timer Added ability to write playback progress to a file Improved recovery from corrupted audio with the ability to refresh the episode Improvements to episode cueing, VoiceOver hints, feed refresh visibility, downloads, notifications, iCloud syncing, performance, and responsiveness Accessibility and performance improvements Added offline guide explaining how the app's cueing features work Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Michael Babcock Earshot Podcasts on AppleVis Earshot Podcasts on the App Store Sonarpad From the App Store: Sonarpad Mobile brings documents, news, podcasts, radio, routes, weather and accessible tools together in one app. Sonarpad Mobile is an app designed to read, listen with text-to-speech, search and organise content in a simple and accessible way. With Sonarpad, you can manage documents, follow news and podcasts, search for radio stations, check routes, weather, calendar information and other useful everyday tools. Below is a summary of recent updates to Sonarpad. Please see the App Store page for full release notes. YouTube content can now be played and managed in the app Added the ability to edit personal media Added new audio effects New sleep timer Added ability to rename documents Added "Clear Text" buttons to all editable text fields Improvements to document and news article reading, news article sharing, media playback, file handling, and recovery from unstable connections Expanded routes with support for additional countries Air Quality information is now sourced from the European AQI Added German, Simplified Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, and Ukrainian localizations Accessibility, stability, and localization improvements Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Ambrogio Riili Sonarpad on AppleVis Sonarpad on the App Store Recent News and Views Surprise and Shine: Recapping Apple's September 9 Announcements By Mehgcap | September 9, 2026 Apple has just wrapped up Surprise and Shine, the big fall announcement event. We got new iPhones, Apple Watches, and (non-pro) AirPods. And yes, the rumors were finally true: one of the new iPhones is a folding one. AirPods have some new tricks, the new Apple Watch has some very nice improvements, and even the normal iPhones are worth checking out. Let's get into it. What's new in Accessibility in iOS 27 for Blind and DeafBlind Users By Scott Davert | September 13, 2026 15 years ago, I produced my first "What's New in iOS Accessibility" article. Every September since, I've been documenting what my testing of the betas has yielded. There are many welcome mainstream changes in this year's iOS 27, such as the upgraded Siri app, new parental controls, a slider to adjust Liquid Glass, further enhanced Apple Intelligence features, and much more. The new Siri has its own app, and coverage of it is beyond the scope of this article other than to mention it's much more versatile and can assist with all kinds of tasks from asking about your personal data to recipes and so on. Lots of individuals will be reviewing these new features. As I've done for many years now, I'm documenting my findings after testing the new version of iOS throughout the summer to discuss accessibility-specific features which impact blind and DeafBlind users. iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements By AppleVis | September 14, 2026 iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 were released to the public on Monday, September 14, 2026. This post contains a summary of new bugs and fixes impacting VoiceOver and Braille support that the AppleVis Editorial Team has independently validated during our use and testing of these releases. watchOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver Features, Issues, and Improvements By AppleVis | September 14, 2026 Apple has today released watchOS 27 to the public. watchOS 27 is compatible with the Apple Watch Series 9 and later and the Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later. macOS Golden Gate: New Features, Changes, Improvements, and Bugs for Blind and Low Vision Users By AppleVis | September 14, 2026 Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 By AppleVis | September 14, 2026 iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are now available to the public. (Note: As spotted by AppleVis Community Member TJT 2001 , Apple has also released iOS/iPadOS 26.7 for those not wishing to upgrade to iOS 27.) This post contains Apple's Release Notes for iOS 27, as well as links to all of AppleVis' content related to these updates. Also included are instructions on how to install the update. Apple Releases tvOS 27 By AppleVis | September 14, 2026 Apple has today released tvOS 27 for Apple TV 4K (2nd generation and later). iPhone 18 Pro: Hands-On and Initial Impressions By Michael Hansen | September 17, 2026 iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available to customers on Friday, September 18, 2026. Ahead of the launch, Apple sent me an iPhone 18 Pro for review. While a full review will come once I’ve had the opportunity to live with iPhone 18 Pro for a while, I do have some initial impressions that I wanted to share. Apple Releases watchOS 27.0.1 with fix for unexpected restarts on Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 By AppleVis | September 23, 2026 Apple has today released watchOS 27.0.1 for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, bringing a fix for an issue that caused the devices to restart unexpectedly. Apple Releases Version 27.0.1 of iOS, iPadOS, and macOS with fix for Face ID on iPhone 18 Pro and More By AppleVis | September 28, 2026 Apple has today released version 27.0.1 of iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, bringing assorted bug fixes, including for issues with Face ID on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple has also released iOS 26.7.1, iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 for devices not running version 27 of their respective operating systems. All recent blog posts may be found at: AppleVis Blog This Month on the AppleVis Podcast Note: All episodes include AI-generated transcripts. Transcripts can be located on each episode's page by navigating to the "Transcript" heading below the description. An Overview of the New VoiceOver and Braille Features in iOS 27 In this episode, Michael Hansen gives us an overview of the new VoiceOver and braille features in iOS 27. An Overview of the New VoiceOver and Braille Features in iOS 27 (MP3) A Demonstration of the New Image Description Features in iOS 27 One of the most significant VoiceOver improvements in iOS 27 is the arrival of much richer, AI-powered image descriptions. In this episode, David Nason takes the feature for a hands-on test drive, showing how VoiceOver can provide far more detailed information about images than the simpler descriptions users may be familiar with. A Demonstration of the New Image Description Features in iOS 27 (MP3) A Demonstration and Walk-Through of the New Live Recognition Features in iOS 27 In this episode, Levi Gobin demonstrates the new Live Recognition capabilities in iOS 27. A Demonstration and Walk-Through of the New Live Recognition Features in iOS 27 (MP3 All recent podcast episodes may be found at: AppleVis Podcast New and Updated Guides A Beginner's Guide to Using iOS with VoiceOver By Tyler | Updated September 2026 AI-generated summary: This guide provides a comprehensive introduction to using iOS with VoiceOver, Apple's built-in screen reader. It covers essential gestures for navigating the interface, such as exploring by touch, double-tapping to activate items, and using the VoiceOver rotor for advanced navigation and settings adjustments. Additionally, the guide explains how to set up a new device, manage typing with different keyboard modes, and utilize dictation and Siri for a smoother experience. A Beginner's Guide to Using macOS with VoiceOver By Tyler | Updated September 2026 AI-generated summary: The guide provides a comprehensive introduction for new Mac users. It covers essential topics such as initial setup, basic navigation using the VoiceOver modifier keys, and interacting with interface elements. Additionally, it explains how to use the VoiceOver rotor, access the menu bar, and customize settings through the VoiceOver Utility. A Guide to Braille Screen Input on iOS and iPadOS By Mehgcap | Updated September 2026 AI-generated summary: Braille Screen Input (BSI) on iOS and iPadOS allows you to type braille directly on your device's touchscreen using VoiceOver. It can be activated via the rotor or by double-tapping the top and bottom edges of the screen with two fingers. BSI supports two main modes: Braille Entry Mode for typing text and Command Mode for navigating your device. You can use it in Tabletop mode (device flat) or Screen Away mode (screen facing away), and it includes various gestures for spacing, deleting, and switching between modes. en.title: Lexo Offline AI Voice Keyboard
en.summary: Lexo is a private AI keyboard for Android. Voice typing and next-word prediction both run entirely on device, so once setup is done the keyboard…
en.body:
Published 1 October 2026 by Warren Carr

Lexo is a private AI keyboard for Android. Voice typing and next-word prediction both run entirely on device, so once setup is done the keyboard keeps working with no internet connection, in airplane mode, and anywhere the signal drops.

After installing, open Lexo once to switch it on. The app walks you through it: pick your language, turn Lexo on in Android’s keyboard settings, make it your keyboard, then try it out.

Cloud keyboards send what you type to a server and wait for the answer. Lexo puts the models on your phone instead: the typing model downloads once, plus the speech recognizer if you use voice, then they live in the app’s private storage. Nothing you type or say leaves the phone. No sign-up, no ads.

Lexo is a paid keyboard. Every install starts with a 30-day Premium trial covering everything the on-device models power: offline voice typing, next-word prediction, the suggestion strip and autocorrect, and glide typing.

After that those features stop until you buy Premium: a one-time purchase, not a subscription. Without Premium the keyboard still types: layouts, language switching, emoji, clipboard history, themes, one-handed mode and gestures. No ads either way.

Setup downloads the typing model for your language once, over Wi-Fi by default. Its size depends on the language. Voice typing downloads its own speech pack the first time you use the microphone, and each extra language adds its own. App updates do not re-download any of it.

Built on the open-source FlorisBoard project, with open-weight models: SmolLM2, Qwen2.5 and KB-Whisper (Apache-2.0), a Turkish GPT-2 fine-tune (MIT), Gemma (Gemma Terms of Use) and NVIDIA Parakeet (CC-BY-4.0).

Questions, bug reports, feature requests: reddit.com/r/lexokeyboard .

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Following the release of the Pixel 11-series that came onboard with “Rambler,” a new experience of voice typing, more and more Devs are coming up with creative methods of achieving the same experience for non-Pixel 11-series users. Thus, we’re here talking about “Lexo Keyboard,” a keyboard that works entirely offline once you download the model needed for offline use.

I spent a lot of time working with the Developer to make the app accessible, and I’m proud of this Developer for his work in ensuring that the keyboard is accessible.

Thus, the keyboard supports “lift-to-type” using TalkBack.

I put the keyboard to use on both my Galaxy S23+, running One UI 8.5 (Android 16), and my Pixel 11 Pro XL, running Android 17. The voice dictation works similarly across the two devices.

What is worth mentioning, however, is that in order to be able to double-tap anywhere on the phone to stop voice dictation, you would have to go to TalkBack Settings > Advanced settings > Reduce delay > Typing preference and choose “Hold finger to select letter key, then lift. Double-tap for other keys.”

If you use “Hold finger to select any key, then lift” instead, you need to tap the voice input key directly to stop voice input, as tapping outside the keyboard area won’t stop it.

There are lots of settings on the keyboard that you can customize to your liking. Take advantage of those and customize the keyboard to your liking.

The app is available to anyone with access to the Play Store. When it comes to pricing, there’s a one-time payment of 10 bucks. Without the one-time payment, you can use the app with all features enabled for a period of 30 days.

After those 30 days, you wouldn’t have access to the premium features, but even as a free user outside of the 30-day free period, there are no ads.

You can listen to my Blind Android Users podcast audio demo of the keyboard Here

Last Tested App version and Android version:

2.0.37. Android 17

en.title: What’s New In Jieshuo 20261001
en.summary: Version 20261001 of the Jieshuo screen reader has been released. Here are the main additions and changes in this version. Support For External AI Models…
en.body:
Published 1 October 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Version 20261001 of the Jieshuo screen reader has been released. Here are the main additions and changes in this version.

Table of Contents

Jieshuo now supports using external AI models for a number of its AI-powered functions.

The new release allows users to set their preferred AI services for the following functions:

I assume that the functions related to the focused item also cover the corresponding functions that work on the entire screen, such as inquire by voice and detailed description. However, I cannot say this for sure because I have not tested these functions myself.

To set the models, go to Screen reader settings > Advanced settings > the section that is still in Chinese. There is a toggle for each function to enable the use of a custom AI model, and you can configure a different model for each function. You can customize the necessary parameters, such as the URL of an OpenAI-compatible AI service, model name, prompt, and API key. There is also a Test button that you can use to check whether the configuration works.

This feature is available to paid users only.

Jieshuo now includes new presets for the speech output audio. These are available in a new section that is still in Chinese in the TTS settings .

The standard preset is selected by default. Other presets include boosted bass, boosted treble, and others. I will not comment on how each preset sounds because hearing preferences are subjective, and the results can also vary depending on the speakers or earphones being used.

The To top and To end functions can now be used on sliders. These functions are assigned to swiping up then down and down then up with one finger if alternative granularity navigation mode is not being used to move between navigation types. They can also be assigned to user-defined gestures and can be found in the main menu.

When a slider is focused, To top moves it to its minimum value, while To end moves it to its maximum value.

Like other slider adjustment mechanisms, these functions work only on sliders that the screen reader can modify.

During my testing, To end could not move the brightness slider all the way to its maximum value and stopped at 63%. However, it worked correctly on another slider.

Jieshuo now allows users to stop automatic notification reading in three additional situations: when Do not disturb mode is on, when media is playing, and when Jieshuo timers are active.

These options are available in Notification reading settings.

I cannot comment on how reliably these options work because I do not use automatic notification reading on the device I tested with.

After translation functions stopped working because of changes on Google’s end, the new version includes the necessary modifications for translation to work normally again.

The translation issue also affected some AI-related functions, such as image descriptions. These functions use translation to automatically translate results that come in Chinese from vivo AI services into the user’s target language.

I am not sure if this change was introduced earlier. Another user alerted me to it in this version, and I no longer have an older version installed for comparison.

It is now possible to extend the duration of the long press and hold function, which is 59 seconds by default, by tapping the screen once or performing any onscreen gesture. This removes the 59-second limit. To release the button, the user must tap the screen again with one finger. Other gestures do not work to release the button.

I do not know if the button is eventually released after a certain amount of time, but I tested it for 2 minutes and 39 seconds without the button being released.

Note that if the user performs the function again while still in the window, the limitation remains lifted. Only one tap is required to release the button.

Jieshuo no longer automatically moves between home screen pages when automatic page scrolling is disabled. I tested this with Lawnchair, but I do not know whether it works reliably with all launchers.

The changelog also mentions fixes for bugs related to some devices, including Vivo devices and others.

A 20% discount is currently available on all Jieshuo plans. The discount is active until October 5.

Published in News

en.title: RealTime AI Cam
en.summary: RealTime AI Cam tells you what your camera is pointed at, out loud, and every part of it runs on your phone. No account, no…
en.body:
Published 30 September 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

RealTime AI Cam tells you what your camera is pointed at, out loud, and every part of it runs on your phone. No account, no ads, nothing to buy. It works in airplane mode, on a subway, or in another country with no data, and nothing the camera sees ever leaves the device.

WHAT IT DOES

LANGUAGES Built for English speakers. It reads English, and translates printed Spanish into English with no internet at all. Other languages download once from Google, then work offline too.

WORKS WITH TALKBACK Every button is labeled, so you can run the whole app without seeing the screen. Nothing is buried behind a gesture you have to discover, and the app tells you what it is doing while it works.

HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS The models are small enough to live on your phone, which is exactly why it works with no signal, and it does get things wrong sometimes. It tells you when it is unsure instead of guessing confidently at you.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN

GOOD FOR

Built by one person at Nice Dreamz in Northern California, and the same app is on iPhone. Most of what is in here came from blind and low vision users emailing me and me building it that night. If something does not work with TalkBack, or you want it to do something it does not do yet, email ma ** @ ******* mp.com .

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The most interesting feature of the app is the Help Me Aim feature, which tries to help blind users with the challenge of taking photos. During my testing, the app was able to take photos that included the subject I wanted to focus on, and the guidance was good overall. However, the subject is not always centred in the photo. For example, when taking a photo of a plant on a table, other furniture in the room was also captured along with the plant. The plant was present but was not at the centre of the photo. I captured photos of a few subjects and confirmed with sighted users that they were present in the photos.

After the photo is captured, a description is generated, and I find the descriptions decent for an offline model. You can also describe a scene using the dedicated What's This feature. After the scene is described, you can ask additional questions either through voice or by typing. You can also save the photo if you find the scene worth keeping.

I found that the object detection often hallucinates objects that aren't present.

Although the app reads the guidance automatically, this is not the case in some other areas. For example, in the text reading feature, which is labeled as English Text to Speech, you have to focus the Detected text item for it to read the recognized text automatically. Also, answers to questions are not read automatically. You have to find them on the screen. My main testing screen reader is Jieshuo, but things could be different with TalkBack.

Overall, the app deserves attention and testing, especially since the developer has shown a clear willingness to improve it, and he is offering it for free without ads. Privacy is also respected because all processing is done offline using the installed on-device model. Speaking of processing, speed might be different across devices. On my Honor 600 Pro, the speed is rather acceptable, both when analysing the view and when answering questions.

Disponible el número 50 de “Arroba Sonora”, el podcast de tecnología del CTI, que puede descargarse desde el Gestor ONCE de Libros Digitales, el ClubONCE o escucharse a través de las principales plataformas de podcast o desde la Web del CTI.

En este número, con el que “Arroba Sonora” alcanza su edición número 50, se comienza repasando las principales novedades en materia de accesibilidad que incorpora iOS 27 . Se analizarán algunas de las nuevas funciones y mejoras que pueden resultar de especial interés para las personas con ceguera o deficiencia visual grave, así como otros cambios relacionados con la accesibilidad y el uso de los dispositivos de Apple.

A continuación, se presenta TagFit , una aplicación pensada para etiquetar y organizar productos. Durante el episodio se explicará en qué consiste esta herramienta, cuáles son sus principales funcionalidades y de qué manera puede facilitar la identificación, clasificación y organización de distintos productos en el día a día.

También se ofrece una comparativa de las aplicaciones móviles de diferentes cadenas de supermercados e hipermercados para realizar la compra. Se analizarán sus principales características y, especialmente, su grado de accesibilidad y facilidad de uso para las personas con ceguera o deficiencia visual grave, prestando atención a aspectos como la navegación, la identificación de productos, la gestión de la cesta y el proceso de compra.

La edición se completa con la presentación del chatbot de Aena para WhatsApp , una herramienta que permite consultar información relacionada con vuelos y aeropuertos a través de esta popular aplicación de mensajería. Se explicará su funcionamiento y las posibilidades que ofrece para obtener información útil antes y durante un viaje.

El contenido íntegro de “Arroba Sonora” en formato texto puede descargarse desde el Gestor ONCE de Libros Digitales, o consultarse en la sección correspondiente de “Arroba Sonora” dentro de la Web del CTI.

es.title: Ya disponible la tercera beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 3 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la tercera beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la tercera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 3 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 3 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es ca17ceb9cd3a8ed7b9732d2a6856c2c3979fbfd86fde1dad91a8a7170dcec612. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la tercera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Announcing AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month for September 2026: Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve
en.summary: Welcome to the September 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve . September 2026 has been one of those months where choosing just one App Pick of the Month has been especially difficult. It has felt like one of the busiest months I can remember on AppleVis, particularly when it comes to games. There have been so many new apps and games to check out, and several could easily have earned this month's spot. But after considering all the options, I kept coming back to Restaurant Rush. About Restaurant Rush Restaurant Rush is a restaurant simulation game that combines time management, strategy, and progression. You take customer orders, prepare food, serve customers (before their patience runs out), and earn coins that can be used to improve your establishments. As you progress, you can upgrade kitchen stations, add trays, hire waitstaff, unlock additional restaurants, and work your way through more than 50 recipes. Restaurant Rush includes a 100-day campaign as well as an Endless mode, so there is plenty to keep you busy. There are also daily missions and weekly challenges with global leaderboards. One thing I especially like is that there is always something else I want to accomplish. I might start out intending to play for just a few minutes, and before I know it, I've played several more rounds. Restaurant Rush is seriously addictive. For me, a big part of the appeal of Restaurant Rush is simply getting to play this type of game with VoiceOver. Cooking and restaurant management games are not a new genre, of course, but accessibility of these games has historically not been all that great. There is something really satisfying about finally getting to experience this style of game for myself, and accessibility is a priority for the app's developer. VoiceOver users get the same challenging experience as those with sight, with some thoughtful additions specific to making gameplay accessible. When VoiceOver is detected, the game can suggest accessibility settings, including a more relaxed pace that gives you additional time to react. But relaxed doesn't necessarily mean easy. Customers can still lose patience, orders still need to be prepared and delivered, and things can definitely get hectic. And that's actually part of what makes the game so much fun for me. I'm not looking for a game that plays itself just because it's accessible. I want something I can learn, get better at, and occasionally feel a little pressure while playing. Restaurant Rush gives me that feeling of wanting to try again, improve my score, earn more coins, make another upgrade, and see what happens next. Something else has made this month's App Pick especially enjoyable for me, and it goes beyond Restaurant Rush itself. Restaurant Rush has taken AppleVis by storm, and a big part of that is because of how the developer has gotten involved with the community. The developer of Restaurant Rush has been especially active in the discussion in the App Directory entry; players have reported accessibility issues, asked questions, and suggested improvements, and the developer has been responding directly to that feedback with enthusiastic engagement. This is truly wonderful to see, and I love it when a developer treats accessibility as an ongoing commitment, not a finished product. Why I’m Picking Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve This Month This was not an easy month to choose just one app. September brought an impressive number of new additions to the AppleVis App Directory, especially games, and there were several that I seriously considered for this month's pick. Restaurant Rush ultimately won me over because it combines several things I enjoy: accessibility, strategy, progression, challenge, and, most importantly, fun. It's the kind of game where I tell myself I'm going to play one more round, only to discover that "one more round" somehow turned into several. I also like that Restaurant Rush is a style of game that hasn't always been readily accessible to VoiceOver users. There's something special about finally getting to enjoy a type of game that sighted players have been enjoying for years and being able to experience that same frantic fun for myself. If you enjoy casual games, cooking games, time-management games, or games where you gradually build and improve something, Restaurant Rush is certainly worth a look. Download the App Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve is free to download from the App Store, with optional in-app purchases. It is designed for iPhone and requires iOS 15.0 or later. App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/restaurant-rush-cook-serve/id6773167802 Now It’s Your Turn Have you tried Restaurant Rush? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? What do you enjoy most about it, and what would you like to see added or improved in future updates? And considering how many interesting new apps and games appeared on AppleVis during September, I'm curious: what is your personal App Pick of the Month? Let me know in the comments. I always enjoy hearing what everyone else is playing, discovering, and enjoying.

en.title: In-Process 28th September 2026
en.summary: Let’s talk about NVDA 2026.3! NVDA 2026.3 Beta 2 Changes to the Changes Our International Communities Copying last spoken text Talking about NVDA Show Screen Overview NVDA 2026.3 Beta 2 As mentioned last edition, we released NVDA 2026.2 and dived straight into the beta period for NVDA 2026.3. Firstly, do go back and read all… Read More
en.body:
Let’s talk about NVDA 2026.3!

As mentioned last edition, we released NVDA 2026.2 and dived straight into the beta period for NVDA 2026.3 . Firstly, do go back and read all about NVDA 2026.2 if needed, but otherwise, let’s dive into what is coming up in NVDA 2026.3:

This release includes significant performance improvements, improvements to NVDA’s dialogs, and expanded touch screen input.

Several performance improvements have been made to reduce lag and improve responsiveness. NVDA now fetches and caches more information about controls in the background, improving performance in controls such as combo boxes and File Explorer. NVDA no longer causes File Explorer or other applications to crash when NVDA is exited or restarted. NVDA now recovers more quickly when an application stops responding, and will no longer freeze or flood the log with errors from unresponsive applications. In live text regions, such as terminals, NVDA no longer freezes when substantial amounts of text are dumped to the screen.

Context menus and keyboard shortcuts have been added to the Configuration Profiles, Input Gestures, and Speech Dictionaries dialogs, making these dialogs easier to use with the keyboard. It is also now possible to change an existing gesture directly in the Input Gestures dialog. The dialog used to present browsable messages has been modernized and now better supports resizing, maximizing, and minimizing.

Touch screen input has been significantly expanded. Sequential two-flick gestures now combine two flicks in quick succession into a single gesture, greatly increasing the number of bindable touch gestures. Edge gestures are also now supported, allowing gestures that begin within 15 mm of any screen edge to be bound independently from the same gesture performed in the centre of the screen.

A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the centre of the magnified view. Windows OCR can now be used while the Screen Curtain or NVDA’s built-in Magnifier is active.

Liblouis has been updated with new Elfdalian, Sami, Maori, New Zealand Unified English Braille, and Haitian Creole braille tables, a Norwegian table for Spanish text, and additional Swedish 6 and 8 dot variants. eSpeak NG has been updated with added support for Ligurian and Abkhaz.

Updates to translations Fix bug with Magnifier’s “Show screen overview” feature when using relative tracking mode Updated eSpeak In browse mode, alt+upArrow and alt+downArrow now collapse or expand combo boxes in more situations Prevent flashing from shifting magnifier colour filters to reduce seizure risk Update to the Chinese Word Segmentation library cppjieba to fix startup crashes from Chinese paths

If you’ve looked at the changes document for the NVDA 2026.3 betas , you might have noticed a change to the formatting. Or rather, some new formatting. Instead of having a list of features, and then breaking that up into sub-lists of Braille features and Touch Screen features and Browse mode features, we’ve made them headings:

“What’s new in NVDA” is at the top of the document and is a heading level 1 – press shift+1 to jump back to that from anywhere (or control+home since it’s at the top of the document). The version of NVDA, “2026.3”, “2026.2” etc, is a heading level 2. Press 2 to jump to the next older version of NVDA, or shift+2 to jump back to the start of the current version, or next newest version of NVDA. “New features”, “Changes”, “Bug Fixes”, “Changes for Developers”, “Security fixes”, and “Important notes” are all Heading level 3. sub-headings in the section, new features, changes, etc, are heading level 4. In the “New Features” for NVDA 2026.3 for instance, press 4 to jump to “Braille”, “Touch Screen Input”, “Browse Mode”, which are all sections of new features for this version.

If you are used to simply arrowing down through the list and reading each feature, that still works as it did. Or if you press i to jump between list items, that will still work, although you will miss the heading. If you navigate like that and hear “List with x items” and you’re not sure what the list is, press shift+h to jump to the previous heading (at any level) and it will move to the heading just before the list. As something new, we’re interested in what you think – good or bad. It’s the first time we’ve changed the formatting in awhile (though not the first at all, though the last change will not have been as noticeable to all our users).

While we’ve been sprucing things up, we recently gave the “ Connect with the NVDA Community ” page a once over. Firstly, we made sure all the links worked and followed up those with problems. As a result of that, we’ve removed a couple in consultation with their owners (Finnish and Swedish particularly) and added a couple more we had found along the way (Hi to our friends from the Brazilian Portuguese site!)

We also took the opportunity to add headings at H3 for each language, so you can jump or link to the Romanian resources directly now.

We’re always interested in adding new resources to the list. Are you aware of any other groups we’re not aware of? Particularly in languages not yet listed there. Please get in touch if you know of any.

One of the popular features in NVDA 2026.2 was the addition of NVDA+x to repeat the last spoken information. You could press that twice quickly to have the information displayed in a dialog so you could read it with more granular control. If what you want to do is copy the information, while you can do it from that dialog, we’ve added a new command to NVDA 2026.3 to make it even easier. Press NVDA+control+x to copy the last spoken information directly to the clipboard. Thank you to community contributor Cary for his work on this feature!

(A screenshot of the original NVDA+x double press dialog, showing the new feature bullet point for the NVDA+control+x command. Note the dialog has white text on black, because I had the magnifier running with colours inverted when I took the screenshot.)

We love talking about NVDA! I often forget to mention interviews here, but we’ve recently done a couple I thought I’d share:

Access Point Firstly, our “Access Point” collaboration with World Services for the Blind continues with the second in our podcast series, on everything new in NVDA 2026.2.

Tek Talk Next, Training & Support Manager Quentin was on Tek Talk , again covering everything new with NVDA.

And, on a slightly different topic NOT involving us talking – but if YOU love talking about NVDA, accessibility and navigation, Monash University, in Australia, are offering a paid PhD Scholarship in Communication and Navigation for Blind and Low Vision People .

Monash are looking for a linguist or researcher with a related background to investigate how Blind and Low Vision people navigate the world using technology.

The project focuses on video ethnography, multimodal communication, and users’ experiences of navigation technology, with opportunities to collaborate with researchers in assistive technology and AI.

This is open to both Australians and International applicants It’s also part of the Monash Assistive Technology and Society Centre (MATS) and Monash AI Institute so the successful applicant will have lots of opportunity to collaborate with technologists about building better navigational tech going forward.

Do refer to the position description at Monash for all the details.

One of the features of the magnifier we didn’t mention much last time is the Show Entire Screen Overview. Since one of the fixes in the latest NVDA 2026.3 beta is a fix involving this feature, I thought it was worth a mention. So firstly, the fix is that it WILL now work if using relative tracking mode – so if you prefer that magnifier tracking mode, you might want to upgrade before trying it out.

With the magnifier running, press NVDA+shift+L to “Show entire screen”. This temporarily zooms out to show the whole screen (as if the magnifier wasn’t running). After a couple of seconds without the mouse moving, the view zooms back in again.

Because the view smoothly zooms out and then back in again, it makes it easier to tell where the zoomed area is in relation to the whole screen. By waiting for mouse movement to stop, it allows a user to explore the unmagnified view and then smoothly zooms in to where the focus currently is.

If you wish to instantly enable or disable the magnifier, NVDA+shift+w will do this immediately, without zoom out (and then only magnifies again once you press NVDA+shift+w again).

Another difference is that pressing NVDA+shift+L zooms out but leaves any colour filtering enabled. If you wish to quickly zoom out and remove colour filtering, then you may find turning off the magnifier ( NVDA+shift+w ) works better.

And a related tip – if you don’t want magnification BUT do want colour filtering, you can enable the magnifier, enable colour filtering ( NVDA+shift+i ) and then zoom out to 1x ( NVDA+shift+minus ).

That’s all for this week. A little longer than it sometimes is, but there we covered quite a few keystrokes – did you learn any new ones? Surely at least NVDA+control+x ? Do try out the latest 2026.3 beta, and some of those commands. Do please keep giving feedback on the changes and improvements. Also please do share any other international communities we aren’t yet aware of.

en.body:
Published 26 September 2026 by neirin

PlayNook Interactive Audiobook is an interactive audiobook and story-game app where you listen to narrated stories and make choices that shape what happens next.

Professional voice actors narrate the story while music and sound design build the scene. At key moments, the story pauses and asks you to choose what to do. Choices can be made by tapping or speaking aloud.

The catalog includes fantasy, mystery, horror, romance, and other genres, with original stories, partnerships, community stories, and shorter one-chapter adventures. First chapters are free, with additional content available through in-app purchases.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The user interface is completely accessible with TalkBack. The main issue reported during story playback is that the state of the play/pause button is announced as each story segment appears and starts playing. On the submitted Samsung device, TalkBack audio is shifted to the phone's internal speakers instead of remaining on the connected headset with the rest of the audio. When the dice appears, an indicator is announced, but TalkBack does not explain that the dice can be rolled or clearly announce that it has appeared.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

App version 3.1.3. Samsung Galaxy S23, Android 16, One UI 8.5.

Published 26 September 2026 by The Podcast App

The Podcast App is a podcast player for audio and video by Magnolia Apps. It lets you play audio and video podcasts in one app, download episodes for offline listening, adjust playback speed, skip silence, jump between chapters, and use a sleep timer.

You can add a show by RSS or search, follow the shows you want, and import or export subscriptions using OPML. You can start listening without an account and sign in if you want synchronization across devices.

On supported shows, when you skip forward during a known ad break, one tap can jump to where the show resumes. This is never automatic and can be turned off.

The app does not insert banner or audio ads. Offline downloads and the core player are free, while some optional AI tools require Premium.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Developer submission. We have not had an independent TalkBack audit, so we are not claiming full screen reader support. We would welcome testing and notes from the community, including unlabeled buttons or missing accessibility actions. Please report issues to support@thepodcastapp.dev.

en.title: LiveComics
en.summary: LiveComics is a comic, manga, and manhwa reader that performs the page as audio rather than simply displaying it. Every speech bubble is voiced in…
en.body:
Published 25 September 2026 by Matt T

LiveComics is a comic, manga, and manhwa reader that performs the page as audio rather than simply displaying it. Every speech bubble is voiced in character, with a separate narrator, while each panel can include its own sound effects and score. The reader advances panel by panel as the scene plays, allowing a whole issue to be followed without seeing the screen.

The app streams a free shelf of classic public-domain issues. Readers can also import their own CBR and CBZ files on the web and read them on the phone.

A free account covers the core service with no card required. A paid storage tier is available through the website, with no in-app purchases.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Tested with TalkBack. A comic is a purely visual medium, and this app performs the whole issue as audio: every line is voiced in character with a separate narrator, the drawn sound effects actually sound, and a score runs under the scene, so a complete story can be followed with the screen off. On navigation, the library, the store, the menus and the reader controls all work without a mouse and report themselves to the screen reader, and cover tiles are real buttons rather than tappable images. Turning a panel announces your position and nothing else, for example "page 3, panel 5 of 40", and that silence is deliberate so the screen reader does not talk over the narration. The panel's own words are available separately, in a hidden region named "Panel text" holding the description, the dialogue line by line and the drawn sound lettering; nothing in it is ever announced on its own, so a braille display can read it without fighting the audio. Dialogs take focus when they open and hand it back when they close, Escape closes them, screen changes are announced politely because the app never reloads the page, and segmented controls report which option is selected. Automated checks are clean, with axe reporting 0 serious or critical issues, though that is a floor rather than a claim about real use. For low vision, the reader crops to a single panel, fills the screen with it and then advances on its own as the scene plays, which is magnification you do not have to drive, with no pinching and no hunting for the next balloon. Known issues and limitations, stated plainly: the "Panel text" region is easy to miss, because it never announces itself and nothing in the reader tells you it is there; Tab is not trapped inside dialogs; the library's medium filter (All, Comics, Manga, Manhwa) does not report which option is currently selected; there is no audio-first onboarding, so signing up and importing a file still assume you can work an ordinary form; the collision between the screen reader and the narration has never been deliberately tested across a range of devices, so we cannot promise the ducking behaves the same everywhere; and NVDA on Windows and iOS VoiceOver have never been run at all, so with the phone app loading the same code as the website, Windows behaviour in particular is unverified.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7, Android 16
